title: Josey Rebelle – Bassiani Podcast 332
artist: Josey Rebelle Show: Josey Rebelle – Bassiani Podcast 332 Serie: Bassiani Podcast Added: October 13, 2026 Genre: Tech House , Techno
tracklist: A native Brit with Caribbean roots, Josey Rebelle’s been a London torch-bearer for many years, pulling from influences like hardcore, jungle, house and Detroit techno and building a reputation as canny DJ in the process. Learning to mix her older brother’s collection of records, she eventually ended up playing nights at some of the city’s most established venues, holding a residency at now-shuttered Plastic People, and crucially, a decade-long stint at Rinse FM. No PR, no social media, no management, stripped of all the marketing is a profound authenticity to her work and sets that speak for themselves, bringing the music she loves to club floors and festivals across the map (the likes of Open Ground, FOLD, RSO, Tresor, Terraforma, Dimensions and Aurora Halal’s Sustain-Release). And through it all is a formidable self-awareness, joy and knack for choosing the right tune at the right time: these fleeting beats are cathartic, physical and heavily addictive. For Bassiani Podcast 332, Josey unleashes an hour of high-grade dance fare punctuated by a slowed down, introspective and dubby coda; a chugging, wobbling, sample-heavy studio mix from a tried and true selector.

tracklist: Glaskin are the 508th guests of our original HATE Podcast series.

Sound, Rhythm & Movement. This mix represents the music we’ve been deeply immersed in lately, featuring some of our favorite producers when it comes to driving, hypnotic grooves and peak-time intensity. Blended with plenty of our own unreleased and upcoming material, it captures the essence of our sound as it stands today.
GLASKIN is the Munich based duo of brothers Jonathan and Ferdinand, known for their exceptional and one-of-a-kind techno as well as their residency at Blitz Club.

The duo has consistently pushed boundaries with releases such as the Valve EP on their own imprint, Inertia of Motion EP on Mutual Rytm, Blue Light EP on CROWD, which earned a spot among GROOVE’s top EPs of 2025, or their standout remix of Len Faki’s Gamma on Figure.

With their live performances becoming an increasingly defining part of their artistic identity and another significant chapter of their musical journey set to unfold before the end of 2026, Glaskin show no signs of slowing down, continuing to carve out their own path in contemporary techno.

title: Terminal V Podcast 130 – Aphøtic
artist: Aphøtic Show: Terminal V Podcast 130 – Aphøtic Serie: terminal-v Added: October 9, 2026 Genre: House , Tech House
tracklist: Dutch producer and DJ APHØTIC has moved fast since his first rave in 2019. He bought a mixer soon after, production followed closely behind and now he has an audience that’s streamed his music millions of times worldwide. The name comes from the aphotic zone, the stretch of ocean sunlight never reaches, and it fits the music: aggressive, dark and relentlessly quick.

In our interview, he talks about going all-in on schranz, why he’s always four tracks ahead in the booth, and the year-long project he’s finally ready to unveil spanning schranz, hard techno and hardcore. The mix is hard and fast throughout, recorded across four decks and is stacked with unreleased material of his own alongside gems from VLTN, RiVid, Lorenz B and many more. Rather than stacking banger on banger, he builds it as a story with long breaks, continuous beats and undiscovered cuts woven between the heavy hitters.

title: Anthony Linell – Bassiani Podcast 331
artist: Anthony Linell Show: Anthony Linell – Bassiani Podcast 331 Serie: Bassiani Podcast Added: October 6, 2026 Genre: Tech House , Techno
tracklist: Anthony Linell is no stranger to the Caucasian capital. With a frequent presence at Bassiani since the very beginning of the club, undoubtedly becoming a big influence on the emergence of Tbilisi club culture, he’s remained a recurring figure in the city’s musical life ever since. Known for his work around Northern Electronics and his more austere, hypnotic strains of techno, Bassiani Podcast 331 holds something different. Recorded on a beautiful morning in the late summer of 2026, it showcase another part of Linell’s musical vocabulary. The set draws from the fringes of his record collection, marking groove-driven psychadelic house and progressive-oriented numbers. A lesser known side of Linell’s club repertoire, captured in the intimate setting of the Horoom.”

genre: Melodic House , Melodic Techno , Progressive House
tracklist: Life can be a lot sometimes. There are moments when everything seems to fall into place, when you’re at the top, enjoying life and feeling like you can take on anything. And then, sometimes, you find yourself at the bottom again, looking up at a mountain you have to climb.
For me, that’s how life works. Like a wave, up and down, constantly moving. We can’t really change that. What we can change is how we look at those moments.

When you’re at the bottom, it can be hard to imagine being back on top. But you will. Maybe not tomorrow, maybe not the day after that, and maybe the climb will take much longer than you hoped. But you will get there. Sometimes you just need to be brave enough to tell yourself: I will get there. No matter how long it takes.
And maybe that’s what this month’s episode is about. A little reminder that wherever you are in the wave right now, it won’t stay there forever.

artist: Sebastiaan Hooft Show: Sebastiaan Hooft – The Midnight Project 226 Serie: The Midnight Project Added: September 30, 2026 Genre: Tech House , Techno
tracklist: Midnighters, a new hour is here.

I often wonder where you are when you press play. Some of you have told me you listen on the early commute, some at the gym, some in the kitchen, some late at night in the studio when everything else is quiet. From Amsterdam to Buenos Aires to right here on Ibiza, we’re all in different places at different times, but we’re listening to the same hour. That’s what makes this a community and not just a show.

So this week I want to hear from you. Where are you listening right now, and when? Drop it in the comments. Send a photo of your listening spot if you like, and tag it #TheMidnightProject. I’d love to see where these hours end up around the world.
And if there’s someone in your life who belongs in this community, a gym buddy or a friend who always asks what you’re listening to, send them this episode. That’s how Midnighters find each other.
For once, you can listen in the same place at the same time as me.

show: Ndrx b2b Sophie Phare – Bassiani Podcast 330
tracklist: Stare at DJ founder and Tbilisi music mainstay NDRX teams up with native Sophie Phare for this next one. Clocking up over two decades of combined experience, their savvy selections are the living and breathing pulse of the local scene, a place where both have contributed not just to the clubfloor, but through a number of community-building projects that have stoked the fire of homegrown talent and fixed Georgia on the map as a nexus for electronic music culture. As longtime selectors, the duo bring a shared history as key figures in their respective music landscapes as well as complementary energies for their first back-to-back performance, a high-voltage deck-side trip through groove-heavy sounds. These tunes run hot, a perfect combination of spiraling melodies and glancing drum patterns, bouncy house for the early hours. Pairing activist tunes and a keen feel for rhythm, these two cook up a three-hour mish-mash of chugging vibrations for Bassiani Podcast 330, a live-recorded set from the Horoom floor back at the end of June.

title: Balance Selections 384 – David Mayer
artist: David Mayer Show: Balance Selections 384 – David Mayer Serie: Balance Selections Added: September 18, 2026 Genre: Deep House
tracklist: David Mayer’s sound reflects a life spent moving between cultures. Raised across Germany, Spain and Norway before settling in Berlin in 2004, he developed an approach to dance music that has never sat comfortably inside a single genre. House and techno form the foundation, but the real through-line is rhythm- funked-up low end, muscular four-on-the-floor grooves and a sense of swing that keeps even his deeper productions firmly connected to the dancefloor.

As both a DJ and producer, Mayer favours music with weight and immediacy, balancing hypnotic detail with an instinct for hooks and forward motion. It’s a combination that has carried his work well beyond Berlin, while preserving the restless, open-ended character at the centre of his sound.

On this Balance Selections, the German producer stays true to form with a deep house-rooted 60-minute mix. Featuring tracks from Dino Lenny, The Deepshakerz, the late Nico Stojan and more, it’s an easy soundtrack for a day spent on an open-air dancefloor.

title: Sebastiaan Hooft – The Midnight Project 224
artist: Sebastiaan Hooft Show: Sebastiaan Hooft – The Midnight Project 224 Serie: The Midnight Project Added: September 16, 2026 Genre: Tech House , Techno
tracklist: Sixty thousand of you hear this hour on DI.FM every week, and that is before the podcast feeds, Spotify, SoundCloud, YouTube and every replay in between. The real number is bigger than I can count, and it grows in one way only. Someone sends the link to a friend on a night shift, someone drops the show in a group chat after a set, someone plays it in the car with the windows down. That has been the whole engine from the start. If the show gave you something this week, pass it to one person.

The hour opens on Drumcode with Taste of the Night, the first collaboration between A.D.H.S. and Kos:mo, out on DC4 Vol. 6 last Friday. Sam WOLFE and PETER PAHN came from that same EP last week, so the release is now three records deep in two shows. Victor Ruiz and Modeā follow with Bloom, again on Drumcode, then Zafer Atabey on EXTIMA, the Istanbul label he co-founded. Victor Ruiz returns with Moreira on Arcane Music, and Atlante takes us to twenty minutes, the title track of the Redraft Memories EP on Second State Audio. Gitecdj and Unika DJ land next on BLACKRIFT.

The middle is SS Ventura and Mankraft with Ravalon on Shodan Records, a label I know from the inside, then Marco Faraone with Killa on Artcore, Davestorm with the second EXTIMA record of the hour, and Tech Us Out on Orange Recordings. We close with Simina Grigoriu, Layers of Reality on DCLTD, the Heizek remix of Mind from Caméléonx on Dark Fiend Records, and Connect (BR) with Calum Kieran on Sound Dissonance.

Every one of those artists is someone in this community can discover for the first time this week. Follow them, buy the records, tell your people where you heard it. Small labels grow on exactly that, and so does this show.
So tell me which track hit hardest, I read everything.

title: Woody92 – Bassiani Podcast 328
artist: Woody92 Show: Woody92 – Bassiani Podcast 328 Serie: Bassiani Podcast Added: September 15, 2026 Genre: Tech House , Techno
tracklist: Dutch selector and label boss Woody92 is an artist operating under a distinct brand of psychoactive electronic music, radiant techno and hypnotic fare that lives and breathes the spirit of immersive and narrative-driven experience. From his native Delft, The Hague, an unexpected electronic heavyweight, was only a stones throw away, and the young Dutch talent felt the pull. Since the mid 2010s he’s been active as DJ, holding a residency at now closed Amsterdam techno mecca De School and going on to found multidisciplinary platform Omen Wapta in 2021. The imprint is known for its abstract, rapid techno, with a tightly curated graphic output and dabbles in fashion and multimedia performances. It’s a shining example of what the very best labels can be when everything is taken into account, and for Woody, a “transitory playground for the imagination“. The mission is clear and underway, and Woody delivers his boundary-pushing energy in every set. For Bassiani Podcast 328 he brings rattling shamanic techno to the airwaves, a two hour flurry of cerebral rhythms criss-crossed with subversive magic and organic, ultra-layered sounds recorded in his studio. Stellar frequencies from a true visionary.

title: Sebastiaan Hooft – The Midnight Project 223
artist: Sebastiaan Hooft Show: Sebastiaan Hooft – The Midnight Project 223 Serie: The Midnight Project Added: September 9, 2026 Genre: Tech House , Techno
tracklist: Sam WOLFE opens the hour with Control Delete on Drumcode, and that label sets the tone for the whole show. Six Drumcode records in sixty minutes, more than I usually give one imprint, but Adam Beyer’s A&R has been on a run this year and the selection made the case for itself. After Sam WOLFE I go into Atmos, one of mine, then Gonzalo F with Disconnect, also Drumcode, and Mark Reeve with Everything Done on Monika Kruse’s Terminal M. Reeve has been a fixture on both of those labels for years, and it shows in how easily his record sits between them.

Les Boys follows, my second track this week, both of them tested on the island this summer. Then Redraft Memories and Spanto with Oculto on Second State Audio, the Pan-Pot label out of Berlin, which gets a long run in the mix because six minutes was what it needed.

The middle of the hour belongs to Kaufmann. Easy A and Nuff Said, back to back, both on Drumcode. I did not want to split them. PETER PAHN keeps the Drumcode thread going with NOCTURE before Sheik (AR) brings Needed You on Sound Dissonance Publishing.

From there the back half opens up. Jay Lumen with Dance4Life on Arcane Music, then Carlo Lio and M.I.T.A. together on Intec, Carl Cox’s label and one that has been part of this show since the earliest episodes. Rødhåd’s remix of Edge Runner by Ø [Phase] on Modwerks comes next, two Berlin names who have each shaped the harder end of techno for well over a decade and rarely appear on the same record. Slim Black closes with Acid Source on Hyggelit Records.

title: 3 Suli [live] – Bassiani Podcast 327
artist: 3 Suli Show: 3 Suli [live] – Bassiani Podcast 327 Serie: Bassiani Podcast Added: September 8, 2026 Genre: Tech House , Techno
tracklist: Tbilisi trio 3Suli (three souls) is Kozmana, BMI and Third Soul, an experimental triple act and key force in Georgia’s underground. Together they rally up ritualistic symbolism and blistering beats, taking elements of house, techno, breakbeat and drum ’n’ bass as working material. They’re closely tied to Vodkast Records, the store so much a part of the Tbilisi scene, where their 2016 five-track Desna EP kicked off its eponymous label with a bang. As performers, the trio bring over a decade of know how to hardware driven sets, dispatching feverish beats to sweat covered ravers, strenuous rhythms for after-hours dancing, Tbilisi techno to the letter. For Bassiani Podcast 327, they bring that high-octane sound straight to the booth. Recorded live at Bassiani back in mid May, this is a one hour cut loaded with endurance drum patterns, snaking melodies and a whole lot of groove. Three souls working in perfect sync, and bringing the ethos of Georgian techno back to the fore. Steadily building, never tiring, a high-powered addition to the Bassiani Podcast roster.

tracklist: Pablo Mendizabal, aka Pol (BO), is a Bolivian DJ and producer from Santa Cruz who has been building his path in electronic music since 2019.

With a sound rooted in tech house, deep tech, deep house and minimal, Pol has become a familiar name across Bolivia’s club scene, performing at venues such as Panorama and Maroon in Santa Cruz, Lua in Cochabamba and RCA in La Paz.

His journey has also taken him to festivals and events including Beyond, Tarja Preta, Trébol Nights and Buriloop, where he has shared the stage with artists such as Inndrive, Rooftime, Emanuel Satie, Chino Negro, Morpei, Enzo Amoruccio, Rockstead, Slow Motion, Victor Lou and Charls.

Beyond the club, Pol has delivered podcasts and DJ sets for record labels and radio shows across Brazil, Argentina, Europe, Australia and the United States, steadily expanding his presence outside Bolivia.

Now focused on developing his own sound as a producer, Pol moves between tech house and minimal/deep influences. His music has been released on Upper Records, T-Tracks Music, Top of the Morning Records, Deep Tech Lab, Subliminal Senses, Vnyl Side, RIM, Go On, F*cking Sound Inside, Outsiders Recordings and more.
With new music on the way, Pol continues to develop a groove-driven sound built for the dancefloor while pushing his project into its next chapter.

title: Sebastiaan Hooft – The Midnight Project 222
artist: Sebastiaan Hooft Show: Sebastiaan Hooft – The Midnight Project 222 Serie: The Midnight Project Added: September 2, 2026 Genre: Tech House , Techno
tracklist: Midnighters, thank you for another week of showing up. Here is where the hour goes.

It opens with something that is five days old. Zafer Atabey’s Keep It Going landed on TRAGEDIE on 28 August, built by the Turkish producer who co-runs EXTIMA, and it does exactly what the title promises. Rino Cerrone follows with Afterglow, Italian discipline, no wasted parts. Then Avision with How We Do It, a Suara cut from his Simple Things EP. Anthony Cardinale has been quietly carrying the New York techno flag for years and this one still hits like it was made last month.

The middle of the hour is where I had the most fun building. Cirez D’s On Off is the one throwback here, Eric Prydz in his techno skin on his own Mouseville imprint, and nothing has aged about it. Marco Bailey follows with Full Steam on COD3 QR, which is the label Laurent Garnier runs with Oliver Way. That makes two Garnier connections in twenty minutes, because Garnier is also the one who pulled the Avision track into his fabric presents compilation. Not planned, but I noticed it while I was mixing and left it in.

Then Mescaline. 1200 Micrograms wrote it as psytrance and Victor Ruiz and Alex Stein rebuilt it for VOLTA. It came out on 27 August and it is already sitting near the top of the Beatport peak time chart. Psytrance DNA, techno chassis, and it works on a rooftop at sunset better than it has any right to.

From there we stay heavy. Belocca’s Human Construct on Mainground Music brings the tension down and the weight up, Nikoretti’s Beyond the Edge keeps it moving, and Devid Dega’s Want You Back arrives on Second State, which is still one of the most consistent rooms in techno. Sisko Electrofanatik and Alex Micca close that stretch with Anairod on Off Recordings.

The last quarter is the payoff. Alan Fitzpatrick’s Zero Compliance mix of We Do What We Want on We Are The Brave is his own label and his own statement, and the title does not need my help. Franco Smith’s Anthem on Natura Viva is exactly what the name says. And we finish with Marie Vaunt and Space 92, Go Go Go on TAKEOFF, because sometimes the last three minutes just need to run.

The Midnight Project lands every week, same time, same place. No gaps, no reruns, 222 episodes and counting, and a community of Midnighters that keeps growing because you pass the show on to people who get it. Follow on your platform of choice and the new hour just shows up.
Tell me which track hit hardest. I read everything, and that is genuinely how I build these sets.

His decade-spanning career has seen his purist production work find its voice on labels like Omar S’s FXHE and Carl Craig’s Planet E, and more recently a home on his self-run DeepLabs imprint, a channel for hope in a world that has it in short supply. His sets too are a demonstration of his tight mixing and faculty for layering rhythm, long-format stints that have graced the booth at clubs like Fabric (London), Unit (Tokyo), Bassment (Hong Kong) and Berghain. His continuing work as music producer and firebrand selector is focused on further sonic exploration, groove-centered and soulful techno true to his midwestern roots. Here for Bassiani Podcast 326, Hess shows his knack for beats once more: syncopated synths and driving basslines with his fingerprints all over them, a sharp selection of minimal rhythms flavoured by his many years in the field. Clocking in at an hour and a half, this latest installment is a testament to Hess’ keen instincts and skill on the decks, a deep exploration of techno in its more spiritual manifestations, boundary-pushing, mind-altering and body-moving percussions from a seasoned talent.

title: Data Transmission Podcast 968 – Cash Only
artist: Cash Only Show: Data Transmission Podcast 968 – Cash Only Serie: Data Transmission Podcast Added: September 1, 2026 Genre: House , Tech House , Techno
tracklist: # CASH ONLY steps up for the Data Transmission Podcast ahead of Love to be… Festival

CASH ONLY is heading to Harrogate this weekend, and before he lands at Love to be… Festival on Saturday 5th September, he takes control of the Data Transmission Podcast with a mix that moves freely through house, garage and everything sitting nicely between the two.

That freedom has always been a big part of his appeal. CASH ONLY came up through record shop culture in the late 90s, with jungle and UK garage pushing him towards his first set of decks. Since then, he has spent more than 25 years working across the industry as a DJ, promoter, producer, tour manager and label boss. His sets have developed the same breadth, mixing timeless records, unreleased weapons and his own edits without getting stuck in one lane.

This week’s podcast gets straight into it. Alaia & Gallo’s ‘Lipstick’ gets the Tony Romera treatment early doors before the mix runs through Solardo, Archie Hamilton, Route 94, Soulsearcher and Bushbaby & Danny P. There are plenty of exclusives in there too, including unreleased music from Jewel Kid & Wh0, Illyus Barrientos x Nesi and Capri x Denis Sulta.

CASH ONLY also brings a few of his own bits to the table. His G-Double-E edit of Fish Go Deep’s ‘The Cure and the Cause’ appears alongside a dubplate from Casnova and his forthcoming remix of Weiss’ ‘Feel My Needs’ with Ruejay.

That Weiss remix is a particularly big one for him. Arriving on Toolroom in September, it marks his first release for the label and sees him getting his hands on one of the catalogue’s best-known records. He also has a new release coming on Jewel Kid’s Alleanza, taking things into a bassier, garage-influenced house direction.

There is plenty happening away from the studio too. CASH ONLY’s recent run has taken in Glastonbury, Hï Ibiza, Studio 338, Ministry of Sound and Defected Festivals, and this weekend he joins the Love to be… Festival lineup at The Stray in Harrogate.

Love to be… returns with a 6,000-capacity crowd and three stages of house music, with Claptone, Paul Woolford, Sam Divine, David Penn, Mousse T, Todd Terry, Gok Wan and plenty more alongside CASH ONLY on the bill. As CASH ONLY puts it, the mix is “a journey across the spectrum of House and Garage”, and that pretty much nails it. Big records, quick turns, garage pressure, house grooves and enough unreleased material to keep the Shazams busy.
Turn it up, get stuck into the full mix below, and if you’re heading to Harrogate on Saturday, make sure you catch CASH ONLY at Love to be… Festival.

title: Sebastiaan Hooft – The Midnight Project 221
artist: Sebastiaan Hooft Show: Sebastiaan Hooft – The Midnight Project 221 Serie: The Midnight Project Added: August 26, 2026 Genre: Tech House , Techno
tracklist: The rooftop session at Tomorrowland was last night. Thank you to everyone who came up. That crowd made the last hour of the night feel like the room was playing itself, and a good part of what you hear this week is what worked up there while it was still warm.

We open on Drumcode. Volkoder and Korolova with “Waiting For You” sets the temperature straight away, no ceremony, just the pull. Tim Kollberg follows on Gain Records with “Pleasure State,” which is one of four Gain records in this episode. That was not a plan. It is just where the good stuff kept landing this month.

Then something a little sideways. Victor Ruiz took Liquid Soul and Captain Hook and pulled “Liquid Hook” out of psy territory and into something with real floor weight. It is the widest moment in the first half and it earns its place.

“Retriever” sits at fifteen minutes in. My own, named after the dog most of you have already met on Instagram. It has been in every set since I finished it and it keeps doing the same thing to a room, so it stays.

The middle of the show is where the groove takes over. Sisko Electrofanatik and Katerino go straight for the low end. Devid Dega on Second State brings the kind of old school devotion the title promises, and Jil Tanner keeps the pressure honest without ever raising her voice. Monika Kruse’s “Morgana” in Patrik Berg’s hands is the moment I would point a new listener to. It breathes.

From Norvis onward it climbs. Jay Lumen’s “Dance4Life” on Arcane is unapologetic peak time, digi.codes answers it with something colder and sharper, and Melvin Spix with TimeKube strip it back to exactly what is needed. That strip-back is the part I care most about. Give people less and they lean in.
Procombo’s “Unknown Force B” is the last hard turn before Franco Smith closes it out with “Anthem” on Natura Viva. Big title, and it holds up.

title: Data Transmission Podcast 967 – Jewel Kid
artist: Jewel Kid Show: Data Transmission Podcast 967 – Jewel Kid Serie: Data Transmission Podcast Added: August 26, 2026 Genre: House , Tech House , Techno
tracklist: Jewel Kid lands on Data Transmission with a live mix recorded at Groove & Bass Festival in Quebec, Canada, arriving fresh from his ‘Explicit Behaviour’ EP on Radio Slave’s Rekids.

There’s something different about a mix caught in the middle of a festival rather than pieced together in the studio. This one comes straight from the floor, with Malta’s Jewel Kid taking control at Groove & Bass in Quebec and working through the kind of chunky house and tech house grooves that have kept him busy for more than two decades.

That experience runs deep. Jewel Kid has released across Toolroom, Alleanza, Glasgow Underground, Abode and Nervous, while his touring history includes Space Ibiza, Space Miami, Egg London, Cielo New York, Womb Tokyo and Sankeys Ibiza. He’s also a Carl Cox Worldwide Remix Competition winner, with multiple records landing inside Beatport’s Top 10.

The mix arrives just after his Rekids debut, ‘Explicit Behaviour’, released on 14th August. The three-track EP finds Jewel Kid leaning into big drums, analogue pressure and classic house touches, from the piano stabs and sirens of ‘Explicit Behaviour’ to the Chicago influence running through ‘In The Dance’ and the rolling tension of ‘The Tribute’.

title: Nude Techno Podcast 220 – Jonas Xenon
artist: Jonas Xenon Show: Nude Techno Podcast 220 – Jonas Xenon Serie: Nude Techno Podcast Added: August 26, 2026 Genre: Techno
tracklist: Berlin’s Jonas Xenon takes control of the **NUDE Techno Podcast** today with 27 tracks of rolling, hypnotic techno built firmly for dark rooms and late hours-

Coming from a drum and bass background, Xenon’s music has always carried that sense of movement- The tempos may have changed, but the restless grooves, tight percussion and pressure are still there- Add his taste for old-school techno aesthetics and synth-led arrangements, and you get a sound that feels direct without being stuck in the past-

The special ingredient is the synth work- Rather than chasing big drops, Xenon keeps the tension moving through repeating lines, stripped drums and tracks that lock together properly- It is the sort of set that makes more sense the deeper you get into it-
His personal pick is **Machinegeist’s ‘Solid Shapes’**, forthcoming on Xenon’s own **Headlight Recordings**, while another Machinegeist cut, ‘Sensory Deprivation’, also makes an appearance-

The mix lands just after Xenon released his six-track **‘Shine Through Tinted Glass’ EP** on Headlight Recordings on 14th August- The record moves through dub-infused techno with a breakbeat detour and includes two collaborations with DAMIANO (DE)-

There is plenty more moving behind the scenes too- Xenon has two collaborative EPs with Michael Rosmann lined up for **Mouche Records** and **Headlight Recordings**, while work is underway on a first hybrid live set with Mython, due to premiere in Berlin this October- He has also just returned from New York, where he recorded his first hardware-only EP for **Blackcat Recordings**-

title: Danya – Bassiani Podcast 325
artist: Bassiani , Danya Show: Danya – Bassiani Podcast 325 Serie: Bassiani Podcast Added: August 25, 2026 Genre: Tech House , Techno
tracklist: Patras native, Hamburg based DJ/producer Danya has been putting out sounds since 2017, bracing techno pushed to the limit. In her relatively short career she’s racked up residencies at Hamburg’s PAL and Bunker Club (Kiel) and toured extensively throughout Europe, sharing the decks with names like Rødhåd, Amotik, Setaoc Mass and Blanka. These days her time is split between a love of music and neuroscience research, a field in which her investigations into the auditory and perceptual have fueled her production work and further expanded the possibilities of her sound. Reaching towards new rhythmic formulations, the 6D. collective member brings a particular kind of feeling to her productions and sets, weaving futuristic frequencies together with a keen instinct for her crowd. In that vein, this next one stays true to the spirit of those peak-time adventures with a two-hour undertaking worthy of her output. A top-notch selection full to the hilt with percussive bangers and cunning beats that roll forward with sure and steady precision. Bassiani Podcast 325 is high-grade techno from a prolific and savvy innovator, plug in and let these rhythms do the rest.

title: Balance Selections 380 – Diego Moreira
artist: Diego Moreira Show: Balance Selections 380 – Diego Moreira Serie: Balance Selections Added: August 23, 2026 Genre: Deep House
tracklist: Diego Moreira has spent more than a decade refining a strain of progressive house built on dark protocols. Since 2018, his releases have carried that approach well beyond his native Argentina, earning regular support across specialist radio, clubs and the wider progressive circuit.
Moreira’s music is defined less by obvious peaks than by the way it gets there- fluid, measured and always conscious of the journey.

On this Balance Selections, the Argentine delivers a set steeped in those same principles. Featuring music from Claudio Cornejo, Kyotto and Stas Drive, alongside a stack of unreleased material from Moreira himself, this is a proper journey into the more cerebral corners of progressive.

title: Sebastiaan Hooft – The Midnight Project 220
artist: Sebastiaan Hooft Show: Sebastiaan Hooft – The Midnight Project 220 Serie: The Midnight Project Added: August 19, 2026 Genre: Tech House , Techno
tracklist: Episode 220 is here, and this one moves with purpose. We open deep and hypnotic, then build steadily into the kind of driving groove that defines the peak hours. Along the way there is a proper surprise: a remastered take on a nineties classic that some of you will recognise from the very first bars. Hearing it reworked with today’s production standards, sitting comfortably next to brand new records, reminds me why this music keeps pulling us back.
The second half leans harder. Rolling percussion, big rooms, open eyes. If you are listening on a Wednesday night drive or deep into a late session, this stretch is for you.
Thank you for being here every week. Two hundred and twenty episodes only happens because you keep showing up. See you on the dance floor.

title: Sebastiaan Hooft – The Midnight Project 219
artist: Sebastiaan Hooft Show: Sebastiaan Hooft – The Midnight Project 219 Serie: The Midnight Project Added: August 12, 2026 Genre: Tech House , Techno
tracklist: Midnighters, this hour is for you.

Last week you showed up in numbers that still make me smile, and the best way I know to say thank you is to raise the bar again. So this week we go deep into Drumcode territory. Pan-Pot’s Diamonds Head sets the pace on Mobilee, then Adam Beyer takes over the first quarter of the hour twice in a row. Alto with Layton Giordani is rave kissed and written in a major key, built from the same vocal source as The Orb’s Little Fluffy Clouds, and Let Loose with DJ Jock keeps that Drumcode drive rolling straight into Freak Your Mind on Truesoul.

Around the halfway point, I slipped in one of my own. Retriever is my new track, named after the four-legged member of this household, and it sits between the warm groove of Chemistry by Dhuna and Pablo Say and the low-end pressure of Feel My Bass. From there, Jay Lumen and DJ Jordan push the tempo before 6 SENSE tells you exactly what to do with Say It.

The final stretch goes big. Free My Soul, the brand new collaboration between Vini Vici, Space 92 and CERES on Armada, dropped only days ago and already feels like a festival closer. Psytrance energy, techno drums, one soaring vocal. I follow it with the Olly James rework of Cosmic Gate’s Exploration Of Space, a classic reborn, then land the hour with Disco Move and Strange Days.

The Midnight Project lands every week, same time, same place. No gaps, no reruns, over 200 episodes and counting, and a community of Midnighters that keeps growing because you share the show with people who get it. Follow on your favorite platform and the new hour just shows up.
If one track in this episode moves you, tell me which one. I read everything, and that is how I build these sets.

artist: Gallo Show: Terminal V Podcast 123 – GALLØ Serie: terminal-v Added: August 7, 2026 Genre: House , Tech House
tracklist: Terminal V was the first festival that GALLØ ever went to, and was the first place he heard one of his own tracks being played. Back in April, he played for the first time and opened one of the main stages in a way that truly announced his arrival on the scene. Since then, he has played all across the UK and Europe and continues to be a favourite artist of EXHALE boss Amelie Lens, who released his first-ever tune.

The Scottish artist has a sound that sits at the intersection of hard techno, acid, bounce and trance, always with neon colours and future sound designs that take you into a parallel world. All of that is laid out on his punchy, vibrant mix for us this week, with plenty of unreleased material of his own sat next to the likes of Charlotte De Witte, MXGN and Alignment. Tune in while you get the lowdown on his journey so far.

tracklist: Dance TV is proud to present Dance TV DJ Mix #679 with the Ibiza/Düsseldorf-based music professional, DJ, producer and radio host Miss Luna. A longtime ambassador of Ibiza’s electronic music culture, she is the founder of Ibiza Live Radio and has spent more than two decades shaping the island’s sound through her work as a DJ, producer, composer, and curator. For this exclusive recording, Miss Luna delivers an elegant journey through deep tech, organic house and techno – warm, flowing and emotionally rich, with refined grooves and seamless transitions that invite you to settle in and enjoy the ride. Press play!

Miss Luna is a DJ, producer, composer, and creative visionary whose journey has been deeply intertwined with Ibiza’s electronic music culture for more than two decades. Originally trained in design, she found her true artistic language behind the decks, relocating to Ibiza in 2001 where she began developing the distinctive sound that has since become her signature.

Blending deep tech, organic house, and techno with elegance and emotion, Miss Luna has cultivated a style that is both refined and deeply immersive. As a producer, she collaborates with international artists and labels, while her work as a composer has expanded into film, including the original score for the ARTE documentary Mythos Ibiza.

In 2013, she founded Ibiza Live Radio, the island’s pioneering 24/7 electronic music station, helping establish it as one of Ibiza’s most influential platforms for underground electronic music. Over the following eight years, she shaped its musical direction, introducing listeners around the world to both established artists and emerging talent.

Beyond music, Miss Luna continues to explore the creative spirit of Ibiza through her acclaimed book Ibiza Heartbeat – 20 Years on the Island of Dreams, a personal reflection on life, art, and the enduring magic of the White Isle. Whether in the studio, behind the decks, or through her wider creative work, she remains dedicated to crafting experiences that are authentic, inspiring, and emotionally resonant.

title: Sebastiaan Hooft – The Midnight Project 218
artist: Sebastiaan Hooft Show: Sebastiaan Hooft – The Midnight Project 218 Serie: The Midnight Project Added: August 4, 2026 Genre: Tech House , Techno
tracklist: Midnighters, last week I told you we are bringing the groove back to Ibiza. Then Friday happened. The rooftop filled up, the sun went down over Playa d’en Bossa, and a lot of you told me you came through the show. That is the whole point of this project, and episode 218 picks up exactly where that night left off.

We open with Per Hammar’s “Shuriken” on Natura Viva Black. Sharp, stripped, straight into the pocket. Yes, that label again. Three weeks running now they have earned a spot in the show, and this one shows why. Victor Ruiz and Kaufmann follow with “Don’t Mess With Us” on VOLTA, a collaboration that sounds exactly as confident as the title suggests.

The middle of the hour is where it gets physical. JLuna’s “Emergency SEQ,” Teenage Mutants’ “Conflicted Mind,” and A.D.H.S. back for the second week in a row, this time with “Eos” on DCLTD. Then Pan-Pot land “Futoreno” on Second State, and right after it comes my favorite moment of the episode: Mark Broom’s remix of “Tropical Melons” by 2000 And One on Rekids. A Dutch classic, rebuilt by one of the UK’s finest. I have loved this record since my Amsterdam years, and hearing it come back around like this made my week.

The back half runs from the YellowHeads’ peak mode “Reboot.exe” into Giorgia Angiuli’s “Light” on Terminal M, the melodic breath of the hour. Ilona Maras keeps it honest with “Don’t Pretend,” and JSPR closes on We Are The Brave with “Japan Air.”

And if you are on the island: I am back on the rooftop next Friday for Tomorrowland Rooftop Sessions Ibiza. Same foundation as this show. Groove first, sunset into darkness, no filler. Episode 218 is your warm-up.

title: Richard Akingbehin – Bassiani Podcast 322
artist: Richard Akingbehin Show: Richard Akingbehin – Bassiani Podcast 322 Serie: Bassiani Podcast Added: August 4, 2026 Genre: Tech House , Techno
tracklist: British-Nigerian DJ and curator Richard Akingbehin is the co-founder of Berlin-based radio station Refuge Worldwide, and the founder of techno, dub and experimental label Kynant Records. His sets draw from the sonic innovations of Jamaican and UK sound system culture, using the heavy basslines and spatial effects of dub to guide his hallmark sound. Rolling atmospherics and pulsating rhythms are the order of the day, locked in tunes from the depths of the dancefloor. Appearances at Dekmantel, Draaimolen, Organik and Panorama Bar are standard issue for Akingbehin, but the weight of Refuge Worldwide is perhaps one of his most enduring contributions to the electronic music landscape. Broadcasting 24/7 from its Neukölln home, the community-focused radio station has brought together countless talents and worked in solidarity with refugee housing associations, marginalized groups and homelessness agencies, and left an indelible mark on the German capital. Behind the decks, all of his curatorial heft and cultural focus distils into something visceral, patient, purposeful and heavy where it counts. For Bassiani Podcast 323, the Berlin lynchpin delivers a racing three-hour dub ensemble recorded as part of the Eerste Communie night in early May, soft to the touch and quick on the pulse.

genre: Melodic House , Melodic Techno , Progressive House
tracklist: There are moments when I look around and see people from different countries, different cultures, different backgrounds, all dancing to the same melodies and sharing the same feeling. Music is such a strange and beautiful thing. It doesn’t really care where you’re from or what language you speak. Somehow it finds a way to connect us anyway. To create a space where, for a little while, complete strangers become part of the same story.

The fact that music allows me to experience this around the world, and with so many different people, is something I’ll never get my head around. No matter where I am, that sense of connection always feels the same. That’s what made me fall in love with music, and it still does.

Thank you for making this scene what it is. Thank you for welcoming me wherever I go, for listening, for dancing, and for sharing these moments with me. I feel unbelievably lucky to be a small part of it.
Here’s this month’s episode. Hope you enjoy ❤

tracklist: Originally from Buenos Aires, Agustín Ficarra developed an early connection to music through Argentina’s diverse band culture. That background continues to shape a sound rooted in house and its various offshoots.

After establishing himself in the electronic music scene as a DJ, he began producing in 2020. His collaboration with Kabi resulted in the Let You Go EP on Balance Music, with its second track, ‘Keep You Close’ featured in this mix. It forms part of a growing discography that regularly receives support from leading figures across the scene.

On this Balance Selections, Ficarra delvers a 70 min plus mix filled with South American character. Featuring tracks from Polo, Scippo, Nacho Lopez and others, it offers an impressive showcase of both his curatorial instincts and Argentina’s wider influence on the electronic music scene.

title: Sebastiaan Hooft – The Midnight Project 217
artist: Sebastiaan Hooft Show: Sebastiaan Hooft – The Midnight Project 217 Serie: The Midnight Project Added: July 29, 2026 Genre: Tech House , Techno
tracklist: Midnighters, this one is built on groove.
It is late July on the island. The nights barely cool down and everything I play out here lately has that rolling, physical quality. Episode 217 came together with that in mind.

We open with a KASIA double: “No Competition” with Equinøx on Arcane, then “The Realm,” her Drumcode collaboration with Layton Giordani. After that it breathes. Pablo Say’s “I’m a Dreamer” is the melodic moment of the hour. If you write in about one track this week, my money is on this one.

Then the groove takes over. A.D.H.S. on DCLTD, RHAPSODIE’s “Void,” and a middle stretch with four Natura Viva Black records, the second week running the label lands that many in the show. Pig&Dan’s “Aptitude” is my pick of the four. Play this section loud. Monika Kruse’s “Latex” on Terminal M anchors the back half, KENZ’s “Blade” brings the Drumcode peak, and JJ Mullor and Gombok Project close with “Grooveaholic.” Fitting title.
And if you are on the island this week: I am playing Friday at Tomorrowland Rooftop Sessions Ibiza. This is the music from the show, played live, open air, sunset into night. Come say hi.

tracklist: Built around deep, powerful and mysterious atmospheres, this mix brings together music I’ve been enjoying playing at recent gigs. title: Sebastiaan Hooft – The Midnight Project 216
artist: Sebastiaan Hooft Show: Sebastiaan Hooft – The Midnight Project 216 Serie: The Midnight Project Added: July 22, 2026 Genre: Tech House , Techno
tracklist: Four Natura Viva Black records in one hour. That was not the plan when I started digging this week, but the label is on a run right now and it shows. Daniele Papini’s Hidden Source opens the show, AKKI and Kaspar hold the middle with Horizon, and DJ Dextro closes everything down with Unbalance. When one imprint bookends your whole set, you pay attention.

In between, Drumcode does what Drumcode does. Rafael Cerato and Charles D bring Right Now, a track I have been hearing everywhere this summer, and Mark Reeve drops a tool called Work that is exactly that: no frills, all function. Listen also for the two Arcane cuts back to back around the halfway mark. KASIA and Shalev called their track I Like It Raw, and after Linska and Duss set it up with Criminal, raw is precisely what you get.

The stretch from Sophie van Hayden’s The Void into Ignacio Arfeli and Tommahawk’s The Unknown is my favorite moment this week. Two titles about darkness and uncertainty, and somehow the most hypnotic ten minutes of the hour.

title: Data Transmission Podcast 965 – Kyle Kinch
artist: Kyle Kinch Show: Data Transmission Podcast 965 – Kyle Kinch Serie: Data Transmission Podcast Added: July 14, 2026 Genre: House , Tech House , Techno
tracklist: Kyle Kinch steps into the Data Transmission Podcast for the first time this week, bringing a mix packed with rolling house pressure, sharp club selections and a serious amount of unreleased music.

Kinch has spent years carving out a sound that sits somewhere between house, disco and techno, always tied together by groove. Jazz and disco remain at the root of what he does, but his records are built for proper rooms. That approach has taken him onto Gorgon City’s Realm Records, Sonny Fodera’s Solotoko, Nervous and EMI, with support from CamelPhat, FISHER and David Guetta along the way.

He was the first artist outside Gorgon City themselves to release on Realm, with his ‘Manchester’ EP helping establish the sound that has since carried him through Ultra Music Festival, Printworks, Brooklyn Mirage, Tobacco Dock and EDC. Add a Duke Dumont remix and sets alongside Claude VonStroke, Kaskade, Chris Lake and Gorgon City, and the picture is fairly clear. Kinch knows how to work a dancefloor.

The mix reflects that. Pietro Pellizzari opens proceedings before Kinch quickly starts dipping into his own vault. There are five solo Kyle Kinch IDs in here, alongside unreleased cuts from KC Gilmore and Drew Pree, My Friend, Alex Mills and more. Wh0, OFFAIAH, Ammo Avenue, Kepler, Boss Priester, Flashmob and Jack Marlow keep the energy moving between chunky house, swung drums and late-night low end.

There is also ‘Pressure’, Kinch’s collaboration with OFFAIAH, plus ‘TR8’ with KC Gilmore and Drew Pree. Released on Walker & Royce’s Rules Don’t Apply, ‘TR8’ is built around deep sub pressure, loose drums and the kind of swing that keeps a room moving without trying too hard. The three friends started the record while jamming on TR-8s, and that shared studio chemistry runs right through it.
Turn it up and get stuck in.

artist: Deano Show: Deano – Bassiani Podcast 317 Serie: Bassiani Podcast Added: July 6, 2026 Genre: Tech House , Techno
tracklist: With a DIY ethos front and center, Deano is a South African DJ, producer, and label owner whose sound is shaped by a thoroughly diverse musical background and early immersion in local nightlife culture. From house to techno and the interesting spaces in between, his sonic identity drifts seamlessly through high-velocity rhythms and deep, driving textures. His uncompromising energy has cemented his role as a staple of the South African underground, where he holds a long-standing residency at Cape Town’s Mødular Club and frequently commands the floor for Johannesburg’s legendary TOY TOY crew. Beyond DJing, his fully self-run label, Knowledge Imprint, has released music from emerging global talent since 2018 and is responsible for debuting many of these artists in his hometown (often in collaboration with VAULT—a Cape Town collective for whom he also holds a residency). He’s released a number of records via labels like Hayes, Hardgroove, Symbolism, and Sungate, with remixes in tow from the likes of Mark Broom, Luke Hess, Tripeo, Deniro, and more. His peak-hour sets are often anthemic, furiously poised, and sonically fluid, blurring the line between palpable spirit and mechanical force. For Bassiani Podcast 317, the South African stalwart brings his unremitting grooves to the airwaves, tuning into his trademark fusion of dark, alchemic beats with the precise focus of a seasoned techno talent.

artist: Illyus & Barrientos Show: Data Transmission Podcast 964 – Illyus Barrientos Serie: Data Transmission Podcast Added: July 6, 2026 Genre: House , Tech House , Techno
tracklist: Illyus Barrientos is back on Toolroom with MALU for ‘Right Here’, and he joins us this week for the Data Transmission Podcast.

The new single lands with proper intent. Big drums, a heavy bassline and a vocal that knows exactly where it wants to be, right in the middle of the room. It follows Illyus’ recent run of club-ready cuts including ‘Never Let You Go’ with MK, ‘People’s PRTY’ and ‘Deep Down’, which dropped on Toolroom back in January.
MALU makes her Toolroom debut here too, arriving with serious heat from Brazil after appearances at Tomorrowland, Green Valley and more. Not a bad first stamp on the label, then.

Illyus has long been one of those names you trust when the record needs to work. Releases on Toolroom, Defected, Glasgow Underground, Love & Other and Nervous Records tell their own story, while support from Carl Cox, Chris Lake, Hot Since 82, FISHER, Sam Divine, Mark Knight and Armand Van Helden puts him in very good company.

He has also turned in official remixes for Armand Van Helden, Duke Dumont, Dom Dolla, Purple Disco Machine, Calvin Harris and Sonny Fodera, alongside sets at Fabric, The Warehouse Project, Printworks, Hï Ibiza, Ushuaïa, CRSSD and Splash House. Add in a BBC Radio 1 Essential Mix, Toolroom Radio hosting duties and his A&R role at Electronic Nature, and you’ve got someone who knows records from every angle.

For this week’s podcast, Illyus keeps it moving. His own cuts sit alongside DJ Romain, Danny Howard, Prunk, Airwolf Paradise, William Kiss and DJ Gant-Man, with plenty of bounce, swing and late-night pressure throughout. House music built for basements, festival tents and those sweaty rooms where the kick drum does most of the talking.
Lock in below and catch Illyus Barrientos and MALU’s ‘Right Here’ on Toolroom now.

tracklist: Dance TV is proud to present Dance TV DJ Mix #677 with Detroit’s own DJ, producer and label owner Mister Joshooa. A cornerstone of the city’s underground for more than two decades, he has helped shape Detroit’s electronic music landscape through his productions, acclaimed DJ sets, releases on labels such as Planet E, Life and Death and 20:20 Vision, and his longstanding role as Music Director of the legendary TV Lounge. For this exclusive vinyl only recording, Mister Joshooa delivers a deep, groove-driven journey through house and techno, blending timeless Detroit soul with impeccable selections and effortless mixing that remind us why the city’s sound continues to inspire dancefloors around the world.

@misterjoshooa Mister Joshooa is one of Detroit’s most respected underground DJs, producers, and tastemakers, with more than two decades dedicated to the city’s ever-evolving electronic music culture. From intimate warehouse parties to internationally renowned clubs and festivals, he has built a reputation for uncompromising selections, impeccable technique, and an unwavering commitment to the dancefloor.

As a producer, Mister Joshooa has released music on influential labels including Planet E, Life and Death, 20:20 Vision, Party Store Records, and Infolines, alongside a number of sought-after independent projects. His productions reflect the same depth, character, and musical curiosity that define his DJ sets.

A regular at Detroit’s legendary Movement Festival, Mister Joshooa has long been an integral part of the city’s musical identity. Beyond the booth, he served as General Manager and Music Director of TV Lounge from 2007 until 2023, helping establish the venue as one of Detroit’s most important homes for underground electronic music.

Whether performing, producing, or shaping the scene behind the scenes, Mister Joshooa represents the enduring spirit of Detroit: authentic, soulful, minimal, and deeply rooted in the culture. His passion for discovering, collecting, and sharing exceptional music continues to make him one of the city’s most trusted selectors.

title: Terminal V Podcast 120 – KLOUD
artist: Kloud Show: Terminal V Podcast 120 – KLOUD Serie: terminal-v Added: July 3, 2026 Genre: House , Tech House
tracklist: KLOUD is a perfect alias for an artist whose take on hard techno has an ominous presence that looms larger over any dance floor he plays. The enigmatic American shares very little personal detail online, instead offering up only his cinematic blend of techno, electro and industrial-tinged house, all wrapped in the mystique of his masked persona.

This summer, he joins us at Terminal V Croatia, where he will again cast his spell, a taste of which you can get in this exclusive mix, which is packed full of fresh, hard-hitting and uncompromising sound that’s earned him a global following. We caught up with him to talk about the state of techno in the US versus Europe, why he only plays his own productions, the freedom his anonymous identity affords him, and how an ear injury has changed the way he performs.

tracklist: Markus Schulz presents The Long Weekend Mix for Independence Day 2026 – a two-hour journey inspired by the universal themes of freedom, discovery, possibility and reflection. Built around the feeling of midsummer glow, this immersive DJ mix weaves together music from the present, the future, and a few unexpected places in between. Guided by the philosophy of where meaning matters, it unfolds through open horizons, golden hours and moments designed to stay with you long after the final track has played.

title: Running Hot – Bassiani Podcast 316
artist: Running Hot Show: Running Hot – Bassiani Podcast 316 Serie: Bassiani Podcast Added: June 30, 2026 Genre: Tech House , Techno
tracklist: Berlin based DJ/Producer Running Hot brings the spirit of summer to the Bassiani Podcast with a three hour, forty-five minute studio recording packed with breezy house. At a fresh 13 years old the native welshman’s intro to electronic music came in the form of rave tapes given to him by a school friend, and from there it was only up. A little older, he set up shop in London where he built a name for himself as versatile selector and resident at The Cause, before relocating to Germany where his talents have since found maximum latitude. His debut EP The Hardest Step Is Always First came out to critical acclaim in 2022, a stepping stone to further releases on labels like Certain Music, Permanent Vacation and Love on the Rocks. His upcoming release on self-titled imprint Running Hot Recordings It’s Best Not to Think About It (out June 12th), also promises to be a heavy-hitting drop run through with more of his infectious beats. Threaded into his sound are moments of 90s progressive house, Italo and sun-bleached disco that find their home as much at venues like Panorama Bar, Tresor and Fabric as on a golden hour rooftop steeped in love and good energy. For Bassiani Podcast 316, Running Hot brings the heat: house perfection, radiant grooves from a four-to-the-floor champion.

Midnight never sleeps. See you next Wednesday.

The Midlands duo return to the Data Transmission Podcast this week with a mix built for proper dancefloor movement, landing just as they line up their third release on Jamie Jones’ Hot Creations.

Their new single ‘Voices’ drops on 10th July 2026, following previous label outings ‘I Don’t Need That’ and ‘Funkk’. Get stuck into Deltech in the mix, and keep an ear out for ‘Voices’ landing on Hot Creations this July.

tracklist: Danish-born, Berlin-based DJ TOOL returns to Bassiani for another dose of frenzy. His trance-inflected selections are a defining feature of his evolving sonic palette: psychedelic, high-impact rhythms par for the course. Spanning earlier influences like punk, metal and noise, as well as newer inspirations from a more purist techno realm, his recall for sounds is unmatched, with years of digging, dancing and vinyl-focused practice forming a bold identity through his ongoing work. As an early affiliate of Copenhagen’s Fast Forward crew and co-founder of Berlin-based collective and event series Mala Junta, he’s played a pivotal role in recontextualizing trance and breakneck beats for a new generation, with queer perspectives and inclusivity at their core. His extended sets push persistently onward, stretching over many hours and balancing an equally driven fervour with steady pacing and flow. Serpentine rhythms that coil and morph through dense and layered structures, DJ TOOL channels meticulous technical accuracy and equally fine-tuned instincts via XL format compositions. For Bassiani Podcast 315, the Danish selector throws down yet another long-form exploration of his signature output. A hefty six-hour run through mutant grooves and unstoppable clubfloor momentum from a techno heavyweight recorded live at Bassiani.

tracklist: Dr. G is on a roll. The Brussels-based artist has weaponised grooves not just to blow up dance floors, but as a way to stir up emotions. He plays hard and fast but always with meaning and a signature bass sound that unites everything he does. Though he wears his 90s and 00s influences on his sleeve, they get folded into contemporary sound designs that have taken him all across Europe and Australia.

He joins us in Croatia for Terminal V in mid-July and before that has served up a taste of what to expect: big and bouncy beats, turbocharged synths and sunny sounds to match the mood of warmer days. It’s a fast-paced trip through vibe-filled house and garage that will keep you going all year long, so stick it on and find out more about the man who is G by name, G by nature.

title: Terminal V Podcast 117 – Kara Okay
artist: Kara Okay Show: Terminal V Podcast 117 – Kara Okay Serie: terminal-v Added: June 12, 2026 Genre: House , Tech House
tracklist: Kara Okay is all about serving up sonic treats that bring joy. Importantly, though, the Dutchman knows you can have too much of a good thing, so he has learned to balance the ups with the downs, the light with the dark. The self-confessed optimist pulls his pianos, vocals and rushes of euphoria from across a spectrum of house, trance and garage, often with hints of 90s nostalgia, and can count the likes of DJ Heartstring and Marlon Hofstad as fans.

His own productions are often the high points of his sets, and are something he really managed to focus on after a knee injury kept him at home more often than he’d have liked. Ahead of a busy summer of gigs across Europe and ahead of him joining us in Croatia in mid-July, he has served up set full of unreleased gems and also shared some of his feelings about studio gear, mixing techniques and how he packs his USBs.

tracklist: Simon James and Adam Helal are the duo behind Rolasoul. Releasing music on labels including Plastic Fantastic and District, they write and produce from their studio at Tileyard in London.

Combining their individual influences and experience behind the decks, Rolasoul’s productions blend a classic groove with dynamic energy. Their partnership is built on a shared love of electronic music and a natural creative chemistry that has developed over years of working together.
Through an extensive touring history and a growing catalogue of releases, the Rolasoul sound has stayed focused on what matters most- making music they believe in.

On this Balance Selections mix, Rolasoul showcase exactly what that believe is- deep, dense progressive. Featuring tracks from Kasey Taylor & Stereo Underground, Fordal, Elliot Moriarty and more, this 90-minute journey is packed with energetic dance.

title: Boyá – Bassiani Podcast 313
artist: Boyá Show: Boyá – Bassiani Podcast 313 Serie: Bassiani Podcast Added: June 9, 2026 Genre: Tech House , Techno
tracklist: Local artist Boya (Solomon Gagua) has been active as part of the Tbilisi scene for the past ten years, part of a new generation of DJs shaping the music scene in the Georgian capital. In 2016 he formed Digital Groove Affair together with Giorgi Kakoishvili, a Chicago house, garage, and 80s disco-inspired collaboration project that quickly set up shop in the city, and became known for its wobbling tempos and limitless grooves, both through their mixes and published work. His career as a solo artist has put him behind decks at venues like Bassiani, TES, Reflector and local vinyl haunt Morevi Records, and places farther afield like Tallinn, Berlin and Oslo. His music continues to pull at the genres that have so deeply informed his work, and picks up those threads to make an altogether new assembly of styles that’s undeniably his. Full to the brim with skipping beats and airy textures, Boya’s mixing charts a course through old-school references and present-day tracks to deliver his tailored musical style. title: Mathys Lenne – HATE Podcast 490
artist: Unknown
show: Mathys Lenne – HATE Podcast 490 Serie: HATE Podcast Added: June 7, 2026 Genre: Techno
tracklist: Mathys Lenne is the 490th guest of our original HATE Podcast series.

For this podcast, I wanted to focus on a passage through tension, hypnotic movement, and atmosphere. A selection of tracks shaping my current state of mind and the direction my sound has been evolving toward over the past months. Some of the tracks woven into this journey remain unreleased, quietly connected to a project taking shape behind the scenes and meant to unfold in its own time.

Mathys Lenne crafts techno as a form of tension architecture. Raw, hypnotic and emotionally charged. Through releases on MORD, HAYES or Mutual Rytm, he has developed a singular language where mental intensity meets physical impact. His productions move between hypnotic repetition, cinematic atmospheres and fierce rhythmic pressure, always driven by a strong sense of storytelling. With his last album “The Poet And The Muse” on MORD, Mathys expands that vision even further. Melancholic textures, suspended spaces and visceral grooves coexist in a body of work that feels both intimate and uncompromising, revealing a deeper and more reflective side of his sound. Whether in the studio or behind the decks, Mathys approaches techno as a constantly evolving space: immersive, emotional and built to transport. His sets unfold like narrative journeys, balancing tension and release while pushing rhythm to its rawest and most hypnotic form.

artist: Mees Salomé Show: Mees Salomé – Distant 107 Serie: Distant Added: June 5, 2026 Genre: Melodic House , Melodic Techno , Progressive House
genre: Melodic House , Melodic Techno , Progressive House
tracklist: The last few weeks have been a bit of a blur. A lot of shows, new music being released, upcoming releases to prepare for, and a handful of new projects that I’m really excited about. It’s the kind of period you’ve been looking forward to for a long time. Getting to share music, visit new places, and see this little world we’ve built continue to grow. In many ways, it’s exactly what I hoped it would be.

At the same time, I’ve noticed something else. The more things there are to do, the easier it becomes to move straight from one thing to the next without really taking any of it in. One show ends and you’re already preparing for the next. A release comes out and your mind is already focused on the one after that. Somewhere along the way, it becomes surprisingly difficult to simply enjoy the things you’ve been working so hard for.

I’m not very good at saying no to opportunities. Partly because I’m genuinely excited about all of it, but also because I always want to do my best for everyone involved. Whether that’s the people I work with, the events inviting me to play, or all of you listening and supporting this journey. I’m getting better at juggling all those different things, but I’m also learning that being present for them is just as important as making them happen in the first place. Otherwise, everything starts to feel like a checklist instead of the adventure it was meant to be.

There’s a lot to look forward to this month. A new collaboration at the end of June, which I’ve included in this episode, Distant Moments this weekend, and of course festival season ramping up all around us. For now though, maybe this hour can be a small excuse to slow things down for a moment and simply enjoy where you are.

Pan-Pot’s Portals on Second State sits in the middle and shifts the room. Alex Lentini and STOMP BOXX take two slots on DCLTD, Can’t Follow Me and Orbital Adventure, with Anna Sonic’s Strobe between them. That pairing was deliberate, their sound has been on heavy rotation in the studio this month.

title: Ina Kacz – Bassiani Podcast 312
artist: Bassiani , Ina Kacz Show: Ina Kacz – Bassiani Podcast 312 Serie: Bassiani Podcast Added: June 2, 2026 Genre: Tech House , Techno
tracklist: Ina Kacz is a French-Polish DJ and producer based in Tbilisi, Georgia, known for crafting deeply immersive and rhythmically charged journeys through techno and hypnotic club fare. Mixing together percussive layers and driving low-end pressure with a polished sense for progression and darting beats, her dynamic approach has made her a regular presence in some of Europe’s most acclaimed venues, including clubs such as Berghain, Tresor, Ohm, and RSO. Her productions too are the stuff legendary nights are made of, her 2024 Endless EP released on self-run imprint Aneelhi Rec, a riveting portrayal of her fast-burning techno running at fever pitch. Merciless, pounding basslines form the backbone of her sound, driving tightly coiled sets and productions aimed squarely at the dancefloor she calls home. Bridging gritty textures and high-impact tempos, Kacz delivers propulsive narratives through marathon sets, intensely primal energies she’s become fluent in drawing out. For this latest number, Kacz unleashes a flurry of techno cuts shaped by her acutely tuned feeling for tension and release. Bassiani Podcast 312 is a trip through her hammering take on the genre, a defiant two-hour edition from a burgeoning creative force.

tracklist: Part of a rising generation pushing melodic and organic house into new territory, a Raw Main production is identifiable through hypnotic percussion, detailed sound design and an instinct for atmosphere that feels equally suited to headphones and dancefloors alike. In recent years, he’s built an impressive catalogue with releases landing on Lost Miracle and All Day I Dream, home to his most recent release.

With continued support from respected selectors including Sébastien Léger, Bedouin, Lee Burridge and Roy Rosenfeld, Raw Main has quietly established himself as one of the more intriguing names emerging from the melodic underground today.

On this Balance Selections mix, the French artist threads together organic textures, hypnotic grooves and luminous melodic fragments into a fluid journey through the deeper end of melodic house. Featuring music from Lost Desert, Kebin van Reeken and Jonas Rathsman, it’s an energetic hour of energetic melodic house.

title: Pierce – HATE Podcast 468
artist: Pierce Show: Pierce – HATE Podcast 468 Serie: HATE Podcast Added: May 24, 2026 Genre: Techno
tracklist: Pierce is the 488th guest of our original HATE Podcast series.

For this one-hour podcast recording, Pierce focuses on tension, dialogue, and release, carefully layering hypnotic grooves, evolving textures, and driving rhythms into a fluid, forward-moving journey. Built with precision and restraint, the mix balances pressure and space, gradually unfolding into moments of cathartic energy while maintaining a consistent sense of motion throughout.

Tbilisi-based DJ/producer Pierce is known for his instinctive ability to build energetic, driving atmospheres, both in the studio and behind the decks. Shaped by one of Europe’s most visceral underground scenes, his approach to music is deeply rooted in momentum: the kind that steadily pulls a room forward and refuses to let go.

With releases on labels such as Token, WSNWG, and Sublunar, his productions are rhythmically precise, texturally rich, and driven by a relentless sense of purpose. As a DJ, Pierce has brought that same intensity to some of the world’s most respected dance floors, including Tresor, K41, Horoom, and Tillatec.

tracklist: Now based in Barcelona after emerging from Argentina’s progressive underground, Mariano Montori crafts music with patience and control, favouring subtle melodic interplay and slow-burning tension over obvious peaks.
Across releases for labels including The Soundgarden and Univack, he builds tracks that move with precision, balancing atmosphere with a strong sense of dancefloor momentum.

From clubs and festivals across Europe and Latin America to appearances in Mexico, Peru, Colombia and Pakistan, Montori continues to refine a sound grounded in emotional storytelling and deep, transportive energy, both in the studio and behind the decks.

On this Balance Selections mix, he delivers a two-hour set that simmers with controlled tension. Featuring music from Kamilo Sanclemente, Nicolas Viana, Fernando Olaya and more, this is well-crafted excursion into mature dance music.

title: Terminal V Podcast 115 – MXGN
artist: MXGN Show: Terminal V Podcast 115 – MXGN Serie: terminal-v Added: May 15, 2026 Genre: House , Tech House
tracklist: Liverpool’s MXGN belongs to a new generation who have come up through the internet age but don’t live online. Instead, he’s been locked in the studio since his mid-teens and refining a sound that hits with brutal peak-time force but still carries musicality beneath the beats. Raised on Tomorrowland videos before buying his first decks aged nine, he has now racked up millions of streams, released on labels like Teletech, Filth On Acid and NineTimesNine and is one of the UK’s fastest-rising hard techno stars.

Increasingly drawn toward live performance and hands-on hardware experimentation, MXGN has been rebuilding his music in real time using Roland drum machines, synthesisers and Ableton-based live setups. We speak to him about all that, his route into the scene, and find out about the exclusive mix he has served up for us. It was recorded fully live on hardware and is an assault on all the senses.

artist: Aaron Suiss Show: Balance Selections 370 – Aaron Suiss Serie: Balance Selections Added: May 15, 2026 Genre: Deep House
tracklist: Emerging from Washington D.C. before relocating to the island energy of Koh Phangan, Aaron Suiss has built a career defined as much by emotional connection as dancefloor momentum. Now based in Thailand, the DJ, producer and label figure channels a melodic progressive sound rooted in feeling rather than functionality. That philosophy extends beyond the studio.

Whether overseeing A&R duties for Outta Limits Recordings, championing new talent, or crafting productions that continue to climb the Beatport charts, Suiss approaches music as an act of energy exchange rather than pure entertainment. It’s a mindset that has helped shape his rise while keeping his perspective grounded.

On this Balance Selections, the artist showcase a crips sound that feels seamless. Featuring tracks from Dowden, Stereo Underground, Patrice Bäumel and more, this is a dynamic journey though progressive textures.

tracklist: SGT is a Berlin-based electro producer and DJ. Built from years as a selector and electronic music collector, his sound hits with the raw energy of punk and the machine-driven pulse of early Detroit electronic pioneers. No gloss, just stripped-down, functional tracks made for dark rooms and serious systems.

Drawing influences that range from rap to punk rock, SGT channels the energy of artists who thrived on the edge- those who blurred boundaries with punk attitude and sonic innovation, like Drexciya and Cybotron. This intersection defines his own style- militant electro layered with analog textures, tight loops, and acid-laced sequences, often straight 808 and 303 sounds, twisted into modern, dance floor focused pieces of music.

These days, SGT is locked into production. Transforming years of DJing into tracks made to move bodies and rattle sound systems, his music carries the imprint of punk; tight, looping structures and a raw approach to rhythm, wired together in his own brand of stripped-back, hard-hitting electro.

tracklist: Emerging from Tbilisi’s restless underground, DJ Sense (Otiko Gakharia) is a 90s-born selector both shaped by and shaping the techno landscape in Georgia. Over the span of his relatively short career, he’s built a reputation for hypnotic sounds that unfold slowly and follow their calculated trajectory into the early hours. A resident at TES Club (one of Tbilisi’s foremost spaces for electronic fare), Sense has come into focus as a master of shifting energies and precision loops. He’s also known as curator and party organizer, having launched his infamous event series U.F.O. (Unit for Observation) as platform for the exploration of techno’s outer fringes.

As host of radio show Tears in Club he pushes the limits of standard dancefloor acoustics into the realm of pure listening, exemplifying an approach to sound that’s not just expertly cut, but heavily researched. While maintaining close links to the city that made him, he now brings that sound to the world with performances at venues like Den Anden Side (DK), Hayfilm Cluster (AM), ://about blank (DE) and The White Hotel (UK). Pushing the letter ever forward, Sense brings his recondite beats to the Podcast, an 82-minute build that balances force and restraint, techno that hightails through murky waters, DJ Sense’s unbending vision for techno brought to a narrative point in constant flux.

title: Data Transmission Podcast 956 – Mauro Venti
artist: Mauro Venti Show: Data Transmission Podcast 956 – Mauro Venti Serie: Data Transmission Podcast Added: May 11, 2026 Genre: House , Tech House , Techno
tracklist: Mauro Venti steps into the Data Transmission Podcast. Verona’s Mauro Venti joins us this week with 60 minutes of rolling tech-house pressure.

Over the last decade, Mauro has built a serious catalogue across labels including Spinnin’ Deep, STMPD RCRDS, Hot Creations, Repopulate Mars, Toolroom, Relief, Glasgow Underground, Dirtybird, Sola, Techne, Desert Hearts, Circus Recordings, Snatch! Records, Kaluki and Nervous. Not a bad little run.

His sound sits right in that sweet spot between club-ready groove and underground bite. Tough drums, sharp basslines, and enough bounce to keep things moving from warm-up rooms to late-night basements.

The mix follows that same thread, moving through cuts from Malikk, SAGO, TWENTYSIX and Amal Nemer, Jude & Frank, ESSED, Cyava and Davide T, Marco Lys, Thomas Newson and David LeSal, Nausica, TCTS, DONT BLINK and more.

There’s also a big one from Mauro himself, as he features his forthcoming single ‘You Move Me’ alongside Dantiez, The Saunderson Brothers and JKLN. With Kevin Saunderson’s family name involved, you know there’s a bit of history in the room.
Mauro calls the mix a “progressive musical journey” powered by passion and selection. Fair enough. That’s exactly what a good guest mix should be.
Lock in for the next hour and get into Mauro Venti’s Data Transmission Podcast mix.

Marcal is a Brazilian artist whose forward-thinking approach to techno continues to reshape the contemporary landscape through hypnotic storytelling, intricate sound design, and powerful rhythmic precision.

Rooted in the contrasts of Brazil’s cerrado landscapes and the mechanical textures that surrounded him growing up, Marcal has developed a sonic identity where organic energy meets futuristic architecture. Known for crafting deeply narrative DJ sets, Marcal moves seamlessly between psychedelic tension, driving hypnotism, and sci-fi-inspired intensity, maintaining a fluid sense of progression that keeps listeners fully locked into the journey.

title: Terminal V Podcast 114 – Vivace
artist: Vivace Show: Terminal V Podcast 114 – Vivace Serie: terminal-v Added: May 8, 2026 Genre: House , Tech House
tracklist: Aberdeen’s Vivace are forging a sound that is unbound by rules, history or pretence. They have an eclectic range of tastes and influences and pull from all of it when cooking up heat in both the booth and the studio. Trance euphoria, speed garage bump and the hardness of techno all collide with hints of musical nostalgia that bring the fun.

The pair only started working together in early 2024 and have since worked without limits. They now have an unspoken chemistry in the booth and a vast vault of unreleased tunes that you will hear soon. In the meantime, read about how they work, where they find inspiration and how they put together their mix, which is a twisted hard techno workout of slamming drums, dark textures and fresh fusions that hit different.

title: Sebastiaan Hooft – The Midnight Project 205
artist: Sebastiaan Hooft Show: Sebastiaan Hooft – The Midnight Project 205 Serie: The Midnight Project Added: May 6, 2026 Genre: Tech House , Techno
tracklist: Midnighters, this one moves with intent.

The set opens with Kasablanca and Township Rebellion’s It’s Chemical on MAHOOL, exactly the kind of statement we needed to start. Charlotte de Witte’s Amor with CERES on KNTXT follows, and Karla Blum’s The Only One on Arcane Music keeps the grip tight.

Through the middle: Adam Beyer with Mark Reeve on Drumcode, EDRDO’s Innocence Is a Myth, Diego Amaro, and Paul Tognelli’s Take Control on Mainground. Stephan Dodevsky’s rework of Jeff Mills’ The Bells lands at the halfway point, a classic for those of us who remember the original.

The closing stretch is where this one earns its place. Norvis and Anna May on Animarum, Demon Noise with Lautaro Ibañez, Amber Broos’s Chicks, Alex Farell with MXGN on HEKATE, and Giorgia Angiuli’s Sanamos Bailando. The set closes on Marie Vaunt and Deborah de Luca with Lalala, exactly the finish I wanted to share with you this week.

Two days from now, the first Rooftop Session begins at the Tomorrowland Store Ibiza. Friday May 8, on the rooftop of Ibiza Gallery in Playa d’en Bossa, the start of twelve bi-weekly Friday nights across the season. If you’re on the island, find me on the rooftop. If you’re somewhere else this Friday, this set is what we’ll be building toward.
There’s a moment around the middle of this mix, you’ll know which one. Drop the timestamp in the comments. I read every one.
Same pulse, different cities. See you next Wednesday.
