title: Yonti – Bassiani Podcast 308
artist: Yonti Show: Yonti – Bassiani Podcast 308 Serie: Bassiani Podcast Added: May 5, 2026 Genre: Tech House , Techno
tracklist: Based between Berlin and Lisbon, Yonti crafts a surging techno charged with rebel spirit. At a fresh 23 years old, he debuted at Berghain’s SNAX before becoming a regular there, and has gone on to play at some of the world’s most respected haunts including De School, Tresor, Basement, Pawnshop and no less than Glastonbury. His tension building sets are sinister and raw formulations that build layer upon layer towards their head-spinning climax. Blending surgical precision with instinctive feeling for sound he’s mastered the kind of peak-hour techno that leaves a mark, heaving basslines with no small measure of sharply defined detail thrown in. For Bassiani Podcast 308, Yonti channels that intensity into a mix that feels both relentless and deeply intentional, a punishing journey moored to the physicality of the dancefloor, a high speed collision of chaotic kicks and throbbing low-end locked in for after-hours ritual. A merciless 100 minute mix guaranteed to get you moving.

title: Dance TV DJ Mix 675 – Doc Martin (Oceanside, CA, U.S.A.)
artist: Doc Martin Show: Dance TV DJ Mix 675 – Doc Martin (Oceanside, CA, U.S.A.) Serie: Dance TV DJ Mix Added: May 4, 2026 Genre: Deep House , House , Minimal , Tech House , Techno
show: Dance TV DJ Mix 675 – Doc Martin (Oceanside, CA, U.S.A.)
genre: Deep House , House , Minimal , Tech House , Techno
tracklist: Dance TV is proud to present Dance TV DJ Mix #675 with the legendary Bay Area DJ, producer and Sublevel label head honcho – Doc Martin. Exclusively recorded for Dance TV, this mix is a masterclass in timeless house – groovy, funky and effortlessly refined. Packed with unreleased gems from top-tier producers across the globe, it captures Doc Martin’s unmistakable touch and deep-rooted connection to the dancefloor. An absolute must listen for any house music lover!

A product of the 80’s San Francisco dance music boom, Doc Martin has been creating innovative, high-energy electronic music for over three decades. Once a mainstay on the Pacific Northwest scene, he has gone on to perform everywhere from Ibiza to Tokyo, London and beyond, building an enduring and influential body of work in the process.

Doc Martin’s choice to pursue a career in music was an obvious one, given the musical family he grew up in. Most notably, his mother sang with Bay Area icons Jefferson Starship. Doc, however, was drawn to the emerging electronic subcultures taking shape across the country. Endless hours spent in San Francisco’s indie record stores armed him with a deep knowledge of everything from acid house to techno, shaping the genre-bending style that would come to define his career.

Within a few years of his first performances, Doc was selling out shows across his hometown and setting his sights on a global stage. In the early 90’s, he relocated to Los Angeles, quickly embedding himself in the city’s thriving rave scene. Not long after, his rising profile took him to Europe, where he became a regular at some of the continent’s most iconic clubs and parties, including Fabric (residency), Circoloco, Rex Club, Panorama Bar and Sunwaves. Over the years, he has become a favorite with audiences from New York to London, performing at institutions such as Output, Coachella, The Roxy, Twilo, Cityfox, Space, Desert Hearts, Movement and Lightning in a Bottle. Alongside his club career, he has DJ’ed for Grace Jones and James Brown, and served as tour DJ for Deee-Lite.

After decades of bringing people together through music, Doc Martin’s passion and drive remain as strong as ever. He continues to evolve, revealing new dimensions of his artistry while maintaining a global touring schedule and releasing some of the most compelling music of his career. A true elder statesman of electronic music, his legacy is firmly established – and still growing with every set he plays.

title: Funreal Future – HATE Podcast 485
artist: Funreal Future Show: Funreal Future – HATE Podcast 485 Serie: HATE Podcast Added: May 3, 2026 Genre: Techno
tracklist: Funreal Future are the 485th guests of our original HATE Podcast series.

Formed by Repro and Adam Askov, Funeral Future stands among the key forces behind Copenhagen’s fast techno movement, a scene widely recognized for its intensity, emotional depth, and distinctive high-BPM sound.

As co-founders of the Euromantic label, they helped shape one of the most recognizable expressions of the Danish underground: fast, euphoric, melancholic, and deeply physical techno rooted in community, warehouse culture, and a strong DIY spirit.

Their sound moves between pounding rhythms, EBM-influenced pressure, trance-informed atmospheres, and emotionally charged melodic tension. Releases such as Hard Candy, Blue Euphoria, and The Bright Light Of Life remain defining examples of their unique approach; raw, functional, and deeply expressive at the same time.

tracklist: The festival season is finally here, and I can feel that shift in energy again. Longer days, warmer weather, everything slowly coming back to life. It always brings a different kind of excitement with it.

These past months have been really special. Being able to release new music again means a lot to me, especially together with such incredible artists. There’s something about creating music together that keeps surprising me every time, you never really know where it will take you, but somehow it always ends up exactly where it needs to be.

Looking ahead, there are so many shows coming up that I’m genuinely excited for. Some new, some familiar, but all of them I can’t wait to experience with you. It feels good to step into this season with so much to look forward to.
Hope to see you out there somewhere. And until then, I hope you enjoy this month’s episode ❤

tracklist: Episode 203 is locked and loaded, and this one hits with a raw, driving energy from start to finish. I’ve been diving deep lately, and you can feel that in this selection. It’s all about momentum, tension, and those moments where the groove just takes over completely. No distractions, just pure connection through sound.

We kick things off with Jody 6 setting the tone on Ride This Groove, and from there it’s a steady climb. Karla Blum and Kaeno bring that hypnotic flow, while Arielle adds a sharp edge with Attention. Seboro flips the vibe into something more playful with Party At My House before Jay Lumen and Devid Dega push things into full force territory.

In the second half, Drunken Kong and Belocca keep the pressure high, leading into TOYZZ with a massive Earthquake moment. Then Pablo Say, David LeSal, and Viv Castle bring a groove-heavy shift before we dive into something truly special, Chris Liebing and Charlotte de Witte with Symphonie des Seins. That one speaks for itself.
Closing out with DJ Panda’s Enter Reality, we land, but not softly.
Thanks for being part of this journey. Every week, you bring the energy right back to me.
See you in the next one.

tracklist: Angioma and BLANKA are a French/Spanish duo based in Berlin whose uncompromising sound takes over the airwaves for Bassiani Podcast 306. Their ongoing partnership brings together two highly disparate voices that keenly thumb through their extensive techno catalogue in the service of an unfettered and contemporary sound. Together, the duo started Room Trax, a label and event series that brings Barcelona and Berlin a little closer together with its community focused music explorations, an underground gathering that showcases both established and upcoming names. Their studio recordings have been released on Amotik’s AMTK+, Soma, Mutual Rytm and Setaoc Mass’ SK_Eleven, and appearances at Berghain, FVTVR, FOLD, Basement and WOMB have put them to the test with flying colours. It’s techno with a solid emphasis on groove and steady rhythm, synthetic formulations that exponentially build toward a point of release. Their gravity defying basslines continue to define their corner of the techno landscape, proving their mettle as innovative producers and world-class performers. This latest number brings the pair together for a two hour journey into their world: a raw and minimal bout of blazing beats and technical precision, red hot tunes from a visionary duo.

title: Data Transmission Podcast 954 – GUDFELLA
artist: Gudfella Show: Data Transmission Podcast 954 – GUDFELLA Serie: Data Transmission Podcast Added: April 20, 2026 Genre: House , Tech House , Techno
tracklist: GUDFELLA steps up for the Data Transmission podcast with a mix that mirrors where his sound is at right now, sharp, groove-led and built for big rooms without losing that late-night edge. With “Morning Coffee” opening things up, he wastes no time setting the tone. It’s the track that’s been doing serious damage across sets worldwide, and it still hits.

From there, it moves fast. His edit of “Shut Up” and that flip of “Buttons” show the playful side, while cuts like Chris Lorenzo’s “In This Bih” and Ship Wrek’s “My Body” keep the pressure on. There’s a nice balance here, known weapons, left turns, and a stack of IDs that hint at what’s coming next from his camp.

Tracks like Marco Strous’ “Yello Kitty” and the Beltran remix bring that rolling, low-end groove, while deeper moments like Parcels’ “Overnight” give the mix some space before it builds again. And those GUDFELLA IDs are doing exactly what they should, locking you in without giving too much away.
This one feels like a proper snapshot. Big records, tight transitions, and just enough unreleased heat to keep you guessing.
Lock in and run it loud.

tracklist: Dance TV is proud to present Dance TV DJ Mix #674 with the Norwegian DJ, producer, vocalist and live act Ora The Molecule. Based in Oslo, she has been making serious waves on both sides of the Atlantic with her distinctive blend of Italo disco, cosmic electronics and timeless club sensibility – a sound that has earned her a Spellemannsprisen (Norwegian Grammy) for her self-produced album Dance Therapy. Ora the Molecule represents a fresh wave of electronic artists redefining disco for a modern audience. Dive into this exclusive and truly special recording with a few of Ora’s original tracks! Dope!

A true multi-instrumentalist and visionary artist, Ora The Molecule operates in her own universe — writing, producing and performing music that draws from the golden era of disco while pushing it into a futuristic, genre-blurring space. Often described as Norway’s disco queen, her work channels the spirit of pioneers like Giorgio Moroder and Cerrone, yet remains unmistakably her own: playful, sophisticated, and deeply immersive.

From crafting records in a forest cabin in Norway to performing at iconic platforms like Beats In Space in New York, she has built a global presence through her unique artistic voice. Her live shows are a world of their own — a striking fusion of performance, character, and club energy — blurring the line between concert, DJ set, and art installation.

With releases on Mute Records — home to legends such as Depeche Mode, New Order, and Kraftwerk — Ora The Molecule stands at the forefront of a new wave of electronic artists redefining disco for a modern audience. Bold, imaginative, and unmistakably original, she continues to carve out a space that is entirely hers.

title: Sebastiaan Hooft – The Midnight Project 202
artist: Sebastiaan Hooft Show: Sebastiaan Hooft – The Midnight Project 202 Serie: The Midnight Project Added: April 15, 2026 Genre: Tech House , Techno
tracklist: Episode #202 is here, and this one dives straight into a deep, driving journey that kept me locked in from the very first second. There is a raw, hypnotic flow running through the entire set, one of those episodes where every track pulls you further into the night without letting go.

We open strong with Jody 6 – You Got Me, setting the tone before Emmanuel Miro’s Monochrome takes things into a more atmospheric space. From there, it is all about momentum. Sian and Sam WOLFE bring that edgy energy with Another Pill, and Sergio Marini’s Freaking adds a sharp twist that hits just right.

I have packed this episode with powerful selections. Westerby’s Human Expression and AIO and HNGT’s No Compromise really push that hypnotic groove forward, while Boy In Nature’s Cellular adds a deeper layer to the journey. Dj Perroz keeps things rolling with K.B.A., and Hybrasil alongside HYBRD deliver a standout moment with Way Back.

Thomas Schumacher and A.D.H.S. raise the intensity with Prometheus, and then you will recognize a reworked classic vibe as Green Velvet and Harvard Bass drop Lazer Beams in that Slim Black Festival Edit, always a weapon on the floor.
Closing the episode, Karla Blum’s Ahogar brings a darker edge before Krzysiek Teper’s Disco Volante wraps things up with pure driving energy.
This is one of those episodes you will want to replay, trust me.
Thank you for being part of this journey. Your energy keeps The Midnight Project alive every single week.

tracklist: I’m breaking my own rules on the radio show this month.

As you know, I’ve never been a DJ who uses this platform to heavily promote my own music or label. This show has always been about sharing the incredible sounds I discover each month, wherever that journey takes us. But this month is different.

After six long years in the making, and what must be the longest album tease in history, The Lost Tribe is finally here. The reaction over the past few days has been overwhelming, and I want to sincerely thank you for the support, the messages, and for taking it straight to number one across the charts within a day.
The album was written as a complete journey. Eighteen full-length tracks, designed to be experienced from beginning to end. But one thing was missing… a mixed version. So I’ve fixed that.

As a one-off for this month, I’ve created an exclusive continuous mix of the entire album, keeping the story intact as it was intended. A deep, uninterrupted journey, stretching well beyond two hours.
I hope you enjoy this version as much as I enjoyed putting it together for you.

tracklist: Draxx (ITA) steps up for DT Radio with a rolling, percussive workout
Fresh off his link-up with Nick Francis on Sound D’Elite, Draxx (ITA) lands on Data Transmission with a tight, club-focused mix that does exactly what you want it to. No filler, just movement.

The Italian has been building this lane for a while now. Releases on Desolat, Nervous and Trick, plus that ‘Future of Dance’ nod, have put him in the right circles. The ‘I Needa’ EP shows where he’s at right now, groove-led, rhythmic and built for busy floors

This mix leans straight into that energy. Latin pressure from Evelio Escobar’s ‘Mi Tierra’, rolling cuts like Twolate’s ‘Afrolatino’, and that low-slung swing on Lotten and Delatorre’s ‘Gata Celosa’. His own ‘Pa Miami’ with Cvmpanile slots in clean, while ‘Believe’ with Nick Francis keeps things driving late on.
It’s heads down, hips moving stuff. The kind that works in basements and doesn’t let up.
Lock in and run it back.

tracklist: With half-French/half-German roots, Berlin-based DJ Marie Montexier is a proponent of fast-paced rhythms with a heavy rave bent. From a youth spent at parties and early experiments at illegal gatherings back in Cologne comes a voice that’s charged with turn of the millennium energy, a narrative structure that both resonates with her own coming of age and brings its newer interpretation: breakbeat and bass-focused rhythms pulled from her many vinyl digs and internet deep dives. Hitting the ground running in 2019, she founded Paryìa two years later, a community-led imprint that platforms upcoming talents whose work dovetails with her own bold and club-laced vision. From being a regular at Berghain and Blitz, Fabric to DGTL, Butik Festival and Nation of Gondwana, she’s forging a name for herself as an innovative selector with an expert read of a floor and the skill required to keep it moving. Early morning set? Build tension. Later in the day? Bring out the bangers. Trippy techno, UK breaks, tribal beats and acid cuts primed for club, Montexier weaves it all together with the precision and passion of a tested talent. Bassiani Podcast305 is a two-hour studio mix: low end rhythms from the abyss, layers of rumbling techno for the peak hours.

title: Balance Selections 365 – Nicolas Ruiz
artist: Nicolas Ruiz Show: Balance Selections 365 – Nicolas Ruiz Serie: Balance Selections Added: April 10, 2026 Genre: Deep House
tracklist: Nicolás Ruiz emerged from Argentina’s Misiones province with a sound shaped as much by local grounding as global ambition. Releases on Renaissance, Hope Recordings and Plattenbank have placed him firmly within the progressive continuum, with support from figures like Hernán Cattaneo and Nick Warren reinforcing his steady ascent.

Having shared booths with names from John Digweed to Guy J, and appearances spanning from Zurich’s Street Parade to key European showcases, Ruiz continues to refine a craft that sits comfortably between dancefloor functionality and melodic depth.
On this Balance Selections mix he continues that fine form. Featuring tracks from Kasper Koman, Maze28, Juan Deminicis and more, this is two hours of well-crafted dance music.

title: Global DJ Broadcast – In Bloom 2026
artist: Markus Schulz Show: Global DJ Broadcast – In Bloom 2026 Serie: Global DJ Broadcast Added: April 9, 2026 Genre: Progressive Trance , Trance
tracklist: For the arrival of spring, Global DJ Broadcast turns its focus to the emotional connection between music and voice; where melodies are given life through lyrics, and every song tells a story. Titled In Bloom, this annual tradition reflects the sense of renewal and color that comes with the season; a journey shaped by feeling, memory and the moments that stay with us long after the music fades.

The 2026 edition marks a special milestone; the 10th chapter of In Bloom. Over the years, it has grown into one of the most cherished concepts within Global DJ Broadcast, eagerly anticipated by listeners across the world. Each edition captures a snapshot in time, and together, they form a lasting emotional archive of vocal dance music.

This year’s journey has been carefully constructed to flow as a single, immersive experience – where every transition matters, and every song plays its part in a larger story. Featuring a blend of standout favorites from the past 12 months alongside forward-looking selections, In Bloom 2026 showcases the voices and producers who continue to shape the sound of trance, progressive and melodic dance music.
From intimate moments to expansive, euphoric peaks, this is a mix designed to be felt from beginning to end. An uninterrupted journey through connection, reflection and release.
In Bloom 2026 is dedicated to the global dance music community, and to everyone who returns to these moments year after year.

title: Sebastiaan Hooft – The Midnight Project 201
artist: Sebastiaan Hooft Show: Sebastiaan Hooft – The Midnight Project 201 Serie: The Midnight Project Added: April 8, 2026 Genre: Tech House , Techno
tracklist: Episode 201 is here, and this one hits with pure momentum from the very first beat. I went deep into driving rhythms and hypnotic layers this week, one of those journeys that keeps pulling you forward, track after track. No compromises, just raw energy designed for those late-night hours where everything locks in.

We kick things off with a powerful opener from Rein (NL), setting the tone instantly, and from there it’s a relentless ride. You’ll hear massive cuts from Anna Reusch, Viviana Casanova, and a heavy collaboration between Pan-Pot and Eli Brown that really pushes the intensity. Sisko Electrofanatik and Roberto Pagliaccia bring that groove, while Bouras keeps things tight and driving.

Mid-set, Monika Kruse gets a fresh twist with a Mark Reeve remix, and then a truly iconic moment: Jeff Mills’ The Bells reimagined for now. That transition hits different. From there, it’s all fire, Green Velvet and Harvard Bass remixed by Adam Beyer and Massano, plus Victor Ruiz and Alex Stein delivering pure power.
In the final stretch, Kaufmann (DE), Leblanc, and Chloe Martinez close the episode with attitude and edge, no slowing down, just forward motion all the way to the last second.
This episode is packed with standout tracks and serious heat throughout.
Thank you for being part of this journey, Midnighters. Your energy fuels everything I do.

tracklist: Native to Germany’s Ruhr region and based in Berlin for 15 years, Natascha Kann has been DJing for over a decade. She spent six years as a resident at ://about blank, where she started to built her skills and learned what it takes to move a crowd. Her sets flow across genres from ’90s house and Detroit to tech house, minimal, and acid. Always guided by a strong sense of intuition and connection. You can tell she’s spent countless hours on the dancefloor herself. Every track is carefully chosen with a clear sense of timing, energy, and what works in the room in that moment. Kann regularly plays at Berlin’s standout spots like Heideglühen, Panorama Bar, and Sisyphos, bringing her mix of warmth, groove, and drive to each set. Whether spinning vinyls or files on a USB stick, her mixes rally together history, community and great energy for unforgettable nights: a blend of rich, analogue textures and dynamic mixing that demonstrate a keen feel for her craft as DJ and offer a glimpse of her city’s singular magic. For Bassiani Podcast 304, Kann delivers a 90-minute mix of peak-time floor-fillers, a dose of soaring, grassroots house from the Morevi showcase at Horoom last September.

tracklist: This week, Pfirter welcomes East-Berlin native MASCHA to the airwaves. With over a decade of immersion in the underground circuits of both Berlin and Mexico City, MASCHA has cultivated a sound defined by surgical precision and hypnotic intensity.

Her style bridges the raw, industrial grit of her hometown with the soulful, driving lineage of 90s Detroit techno. Recently, she made waves by expanding the genre’s boundaries through a live collaboration with the National Orchestra of Guatemala, proving her ability to command both the sweat-soaked dancefloor and the grand concert hall.

For this 70-minute journey, MASCHA delivers a masterclass in tension and release. Featuring heavyweights like Oscar Mulero, Planetary Assault Systems, and Rødhåd, the mix is a tightly structured descent into the deep, rhythmic techno that defines the MindTrip aesthetic.

tracklist: dc11 is the 482nd guest of our original Hate Podcast series.

‘This podcast is a live one take in the studio, using the same tools I use live in a club, Octatrack, 909, a small modular. A collection of sounds I’ve been toying with recently, quite synth forward and driving; I love synths and love even more putting them forward in the mix. An hour of peak time, straightforward techno.’

The Rennes-based artist dc11 got into making music via modular synthesizers and to this day they are his tool of choice in the studio as well as in clubs. Gravitating towards the loopy side of techno, his live sets always leave a big part to improvisation. Finding ways to slightly shift loops hasn’t lost its appeal yet.

tracklist: After a little break between shows, it always feels a bit unfamiliar to step behind the decks again. Not because it’s been that long, but because playing your music in front of people is such a super special feeling. Something day to day life, and the time in between, doesn’t really compare to. It reminds me of coming back from a holiday, sitting down at your desk, staring at your screen and thinking, “ok… so how do I do this again?”

Nothing has really changed. It’s not something you unlearn in a few days. You just need a moment to find your rhythm again, to reconnect with it. But that small gap, between not quite knowing what you’re doing and everything clicking back into place, that’s the part that makes me a little nervous every time. At the same time, I know that once I’m up there, surrounded by all of you, it will feel exactly how it’s supposed to. Like it always does. And honestly, that’s the part I’m looking forward to the most.
But until that moment is here, I hope you enjoy this month’s episode ❤

title: Balance Selections 364 – Paul James Nolan
artist: Paul James Nolan Show: Balance Selections 364 – Paul James Nolan Serie: Balance Selections Added: April 3, 2026 Genre: Deep House
tracklist: Paul James Nolan approaches electronic music as a tool for transformation, using the booth not just to perform, but to hold space and guide a shared, immersive experience.
With a background in high-end audio engineering alongside artists like Sasha and Junkie XL, his technical precision underpins a sound that feels both tactile and emotionally charged.
With releases spanning Bedrock Records to When We Dip, his work is supported by artists including Hernan Cattaneo, John Digweed, Patrice Bäumel and Tim Green.

With a heavily anticipated official remix of Diabla by Funk D’Void slated for release on one of the world’s most influential electronic labels later this year, Paul continues to build momentum as a vital voice in the scene.

On this Balance Selections, he showcases that approach across a two-hour mix. Featuring tracks from Trentemøller, Four Candles, Redspace and more, it unfolds patiently before building toward an energetic finale.

title: Sebastiaan Hooft – The Midnight Project 200
artist: Sebastiaan Hooft Show: Sebastiaan Hooft – The Midnight Project 200 Serie: The Midnight Project Added: April 1, 2026 Genre: Tech House , Techno
tracklist: Episode 200… wow. What a milestone. This week’s Midnight Project is all about that raw, driving energy that’s been fueling dancefloors for years, but with a forward push into what’s next. I wanted this one to feel like a journey, starting deep, building tension, and then unleashing pure intensity as we celebrate this special moment together.

I’ve packed this episode with absolute power. From the timeless energy of Monika Kruse’s Latex to the hypnotic pull of Nicole Moudaber’s Black Silk, and the relentless drive of Space 92’s Dimension, this is one of those sets that just doesn’t let go. You’ll also hear massive collaborations like Chris Liebing and Charlotte de Witte with Symphonie des Seins, plus that explosive closing with Lilly Palmer and Space 92 on Vicious Chords.

There are so many standout moments in here, including that Radio Slave remix of Ralph Falcon’s Break You and the dark groove of Victor Ruiz’s Scorpio (HNGT Remix). This is exactly what The Midnight Project stands for: timeless sounds, forward-thinking energy, and tracks that hit you right in the chest.
Thank you for being part of this journey and for riding with me all the way to episode 200. This is just the beginning of the next chapter.

title: Chontane – Bassiani Podcast 303
artist: Chontane Show: Chontane – Bassiani Podcast 303 Serie: Bassiani Podcast Added: March 31, 2026 Genre: Tech House , Techno
tracklist: Meet Chontane, a Berlin-based producer and DJ with Ukrainian roots blending sharp-witted sound design and genre-fluid tunes for the capital and beyond. He cut his teeth at Krach in Berlin’s leafy Humboldthain before delving into venues like Tresor and K41 (Kyiv), as well as RSO, Berghain, Blitz, Basement NYC, Fuse (Brussels), and of course, Bassiani. Techno, breaks and electro, permeated with tribal rhythms and 90s kick, a modus operandi that sets him apart as Berlin favourite and clubfloor champion. Since 2018, his studio releases have appeared on labels like Monnom Black, Mutual Rytm and Emerald, and a further push to innovate has brought his self-run imprint TANE into the light where his powerful yet contained sound flourishes. Last year’s Set a Dot ([TANE003]) received particular attention for its rhythmic dexterity and relentless drive, with standout tracks Magallanes and Cycle Break quickly becoming crowd favourites. His sound is dense, layered, astute in its selection and unsparing in its demands, body-focused music from the future that invokes the spirit of the early 2000s and all its techno splendour. With a discography that spans over 90 tracks, he continues to evolve, blending UK-style rhythms with hypnotic loops as well as other influences. Bassiani Podcast 303 is a take no prisoners, 105-minute mix that covers all his usual bases and more: mile a minute beats that climb towards their heady peak. As he gears up for more releases and global gigs in 2026, Chontane remains a vital voice in modern electronic music, always ready to surprise and move the dancefloor.

artist: Juan Pablo Torrez , Kostya Outta Show: Juan Pablo Torrez – Clubsonica Radio 070 (Kostya Outta Guestmix) Serie: Clubsonica Radio Added: March 26, 2026 Genre: Progressive House
show: Juan Pablo Torrez – Clubsonica Radio 070 (Kostya Outta Guestmix)
tracklist: Hello everyone, and welcome to a brand new episode of Clubsonica Radio with your host and the DJ for the first hour of the show, Juan Pablo Torrez.

This episode delivers a deep and melodic progressive journey, blending atmospheric textures with driving grooves. The first hour features music from Elliot Moriarty, Ritchie Haydn, Franco Camiolo, Nicolas Viana, Ignacio Hernández, Pablo Arbelaez, Mauro Aguirre & Jossem, and more, alongside a standout remix by Matthew Sona and a special rework by Juan Ibanez on ELECGROUND’s “Quasar”.
In the second hour, we welcome Polish artist Kostya Outta for a special guest mix.

Known for his releases on leading underground labels such as Mango Alley, Balkan Connection, UV, and Replug, Kostya has established himself as a key figure in the progressive house scene, with support from artists like Nick Warren, Eelke Kleijn, and Henry Saiz. Returning to Clubsonica, he delivers a powerful new remix of “Ad Astra” by ELECGROUND, bringing his signature high-energy approach with driving grooves, intricate percussion, and evolving melodic elements.
The result is a dynamic and refined interpretation that perfectly reflects his distinctive sound and production style.
Now he takes over the second hour with an exclusive mix for Clubsonica Radio, showcasing a deep and energetic journey through his current sound.
Let the music set your vibes, and let me know what you think about the show. Leave a comment, like, and repost. This is a great way to support your artists.
Remember that music is life, enjoy.

tracklist: Episode 199 is here, and this one hits with pure late-night intensity from the very first kick. I built this set to keep you locked in that hypnotic zone, driving, emotional, and raw in all the right moments. We open strong with OZBEK and Zafer Atabey’s “Shake Off,” setting the tone before rolling into the deep, powerful energy of Belocca and Sisko Electrofanatik’s remix of “Ametista.” The momentum keeps building with serious heat from Eli Brown and Pan-Pot on “Coming In Heavy,” a track that absolutely slams on big systems.

There’s also a beautiful balance in this episode. Tracks like Sam WOLFE’s “My Instinct” and KASIA’s “Simulate” bring that hypnotic tension, while Jay Crusoe and KAŸ Wagner add groove and emotion to the mix. And then we close with something truly special, Push’s “Universal Nation” (BLR Remix). A legendary moment, reimagined for now.
As always, I’ve packed this episode with music I love, including some real standouts and must-play tracks that are lighting up dancefloors right now.
Thank you for being part of this journey. Your energy keeps this project alive.

title: Ulf Eriksson – Bassiani Podcast 302
artist: Ulf Eriksson Show: Ulf Eriksson – Bassiani Podcast 302 Serie: Bassiani Podcast Added: March 24, 2026 Genre: Tech House , Techno
tracklist: For about two decades, Ulf Eriksson has put blood, sweat and tears into the Malmö scene, and weathered the challenges that come with such a fast changing landscape. As DJ, head of the legendary Kontra-Musik label, AD at Inkonst and chief curator of electronic and experimental music fest Intonal, he’s a name whose fate is intimately tied to his local scene, having helped build the city’s cultural heft from the ground up. Kontra-Musik started in 2002, a club night at first then imprint with a radically open aesthetic that covers techno, house and ambient from a mix of underground local talents. His ongoing partnership with Sebastian Mullaert has seen the duo tour with Mullaert on live duties and Eriksson on decks, a pairing that furnished 2016’s The Dance, a nine-track kicker designed for three dimensional listening that pulled in some of their close collaborators for a masterful exploration in sound. His studio work with Andreas Tilliander (TM404) will also release a collaborative EP this May. Eriksson’s own musical approach is a textural deep-dive into the world of wax, as a mainly vinyl DJ he creates slow-build structures that reward patience with fine analog detail and emotional complexity. For Bassiani Podcast 302, the Swedish pioneer keeps things light without losing any of his broader palette: this is an 85-minute studio mix with spring set in its sights, a fresh and synth-heavy number from a Malmö legend.

tracklist: Deetronis is the 481st guest of our original HATE Podcast series.

For over three decades, Sam Geiser has shaped the landscape of House and Techno in ways that are impossible to overstate. With a catalog spanning timeless classics and influential releases, he has firmly established him as one of the most musically sophisticated producers in the game. Recently, Sam has also reignited his Techno persona SOULMATE, delivering a string of irresistibly body-moving releases on the iconic Ilian Tape.

There are artists who are extraordinary in the studio, and others who redefine what it means to be a DJ — but it is a rare sight when both qualities reside in one person. Deetron is one of those rare cases. Watching him mix reveals not only the heights of technical mastery, but how deeply technique can enhance the emotional and physical power of a DJ set.

title: Dance TV DJ Mix 672 – ADMN (Detroit, U.S.A.)
artist: ADMN Show: Dance TV DJ Mix 672 – ADMN (Detroit, U.S.A.) Serie: Dance TV DJ Mix Added: March 20, 2026 Genre: Deep House , House , Minimal , Tech House , Techno
show: Dance TV DJ Mix 672 – ADMN (Detroit, U.S.A.)
genre: Deep House , House , Minimal , Tech House , Techno
tracklist: Dance TV is proud to present Dance TV DJ Mix #672 with Detroit’s DJ, producer and Infolines imprint head honcho — ADMN. Rooted in the city’s rich musical legacy, ADMN delivers a seamless journey moving from house through minimal into techno, all infused with that unmistakable Detroit soul. Blending his own productions with cuts from some of the city’s finest and beyond, this is a dope, carefully crafted selection with a uniquely smooth and captivating flow. Enjoy!

Behind a Clark Kent–like exterior—glasses, calm demeanor, and a knowing smile—Alexander Drazin, aka ADMN, operates as one of Detroit’s more elusive sonic architects. With a natural affinity for both music and technology, his journey began early and has evolved into a relentless pursuit of sound, shaped by the grit and depth of Detroit’s underground.

ADMN’s style resists easy categorization. Rooted in an almost entirely original output, his sets and productions blend raw textures, minimal structures, and heavy low-end into a signature sound often described as minimal ghetto sludge—a hypnotic, driving fusion that feels both industrial and deeply soulful.

His technical foundation was sharpened at Allure Sound Studios, where he worked as an audio engineer on multiple records, including Recovery by Eminem. This studio experience continues to inform his precise, detail-driven approach in both production and performance.

Balancing life as a network engineer, producer, DJ, and label head of Infolines, ADMN remains deeply embedded in Detroit’s scene, holding a residency at TV Lounge and performing across the U.S. He has appeared multiple times at Movement Electronic Music Festival, including the main stage in 2022, as well as virtual editions like Movement At Home and Paxahau’s Micro Movement.

His discography reflects strong ties to Detroit’s legacy and global underground, with releases and remixes for labels such as Planet E (including remixing Carl Craig’s seminal ‘Psyche – From Beyond’ along side Seth Troxler and Ataxia), and collaborations with Oliver Dollar on Rekids, Refuge AUS, and his own Infolines imprint.
Consistently evolving yet unmistakably rooted, ADMN continues to push a sound that is as functional as it is forward-thinking—built for dark rooms, deep systems, and those who know.

tracklist: Hailing from Australia and now based in Berlin, Leah Marie is part of a new wave of artists shaping the deeper end of the electronic spectrum. Her sound moves between deep, progressive and melodic house, with a touch of cerebral techno; built on groove, restraint and a strong sense of space. In the booth, she favours flow over flash, guiding sets with careful pacing and an instinct for atmosphere.

Her productions and remixes have found a home on labels include Mango Alley to Musique de Lune Noir, with further releases on the horizon. Along the way, she’s taken that sound beyond Berlin, playing across Germany, Portugal, the Netherlands and the UK.

In 2025, she co-founded Kontrast. with Dilby and Dowden- a Berlin-based event centred on the deeper, groove-led corners of house music. The next edition lands at Hotel Amano East Rooftop on Saturday 11th April (more info here).

artist: AHIL Show: Monument Techno Podcast 511 – AHIL Serie: Monument Techno Podcast Added: March 19, 2026 Genre: Techno
tracklist: AHIL joins the Monument Podcast from Rotterdam with a rich and immersive addition to the series. Episode 511 unfolds as an ever-evolving journey, blending depth, energy, and seamless progression throughout.

“Having the opportunity to create a mix for Monument, a platform and festival that has shaped my sound over the past six years, feels truly special. I approached this mix the same way I would approach a festival set, I want this to feel as a journey shared between artist and dancer. It begins with space to arrive, to settle into the moment, and to prepare for the adventure ahead. Slowly, percussive and deep hypnotic elements emerge, inviting the body to move almost unconsciously. As the story unfolds, rhythms intensify and tension gradually builds, guiding the listener deeper into the experience. What starts as a subtle pulse evolves into a more intense flow of energy, leading towards a final moment of release”

tracklist: Pōnky is the 480th guest of our original HATE Podcast series.

In this set, Ponky explores the hypnotic side of techno: driving energy, fluid percussion, and immersive loops that pull the listener into a continuous state of movement. The groove is constant, but never static — small details appear and disappear, synths swirl through space, and the rhythm unfolds like a living organism. As the set evolves, the intensity rises through thicker arrangements and more complex rhythmic structures.

The hypnotic groove remains the guiding force, but the sonic palette expands gradually, revealing new textures and emotional depth.Toward the final part of the set, the energy begins to transform. The dense rhythmic layers slowly open up, making space for more melodic elements to emerge.
Available to listen to via our SoundCloud from Sunday (15th of March, 2026)

title: Sebastiaan Hooft – The Midnight Project 197
artist: Sebastiaan Hooft Show: Sebastiaan Hooft – The Midnight Project 197 Serie: The Midnight Project Added: March 11, 2026 Genre: Tech House , Techno
tracklist: Episode 197 of The Midnight Project is here, and this one hits straight from the first second. I’m opening the show with my brand new track Atmos, and to celebrate the release, I’ve made it available as a free download for a few days on my SoundCloud. If you want to grab it, head over to https://soundcloud.com/sebastiaan-hooft while it’s still up.

From there, we dive deep into a powerful journey packed with driving energy and hypnotic grooves. Mario Ochoa brings serious tension with Forsaken, Pan-Pot delivers their unmistakable signature with Altered State, and METODI drops the wild Prince Igor On Steroids. Victoria Engel keeps the momentum flowing before the massive collaboration between Chris Liebing and Charlotte de Witte, Symphonie des Seins, takes things to another level.

You’ll also hear Amelie Lens with Falling Into Acid Dreams, a fierce moment from Paula van Klar with Calentura, and Tom Wax bringing pure rave spirit with The Rave Machine. Spartaque, Danny Aion, and Pablo Say keep the pressure building before we close strong with Bart Skils & Weska on Drumcode and George Z calling everyone back to the dancefloor.
As always, this episode is packed with incredible artists pushing the sound forward, and I’m grateful to share these tracks with you every week.
Thank you for being part of this journey and for keeping the energy alive every week. I see you, Midnighters.

title: Function – Bassiani Podcast 300
artist: Function Show: Function – Bassiani Podcast 300 Serie: Bassiani Podcast Added: March 10, 2026 Genre: Tech House , Techno
tracklist: Function returns for a new podcast and a new year. The techno veteran and native New Yorker emerged out of the Big Apple in the heady days of the early 90s, think Jeff Mills and Limelight, before recordings on Synewave, Downwards and his own label Infrastructure started to surface. He went on to co-found the groundbreaking Sandwell District collective and eventually landed in Berlin, becoming a Berghain resident and part of the Ostgut roster within due course. The decades since have seen him cement his position as a forerunner of the techno genre, with releases such as his career defining Incubation and more recent Green EP (2023) timed as the relaunch of his infamous label. He continues to shape the landscape of electronic music with a stylistic approach that threads together gritty beats and delay heavy atmospheres, articulating a sound that’s emotional and merciless all at once. Bassiani Podcast 300 comes from his closing set at the club’s season opening night back in September, and it’s got enough momentum and ideas to keep even the hungriest raver satisfied. Clocking in at just over seven hours, this one’s a true testament to Function’s skill and experience, channeling his three decades of musical exploration into a poker hot endurance set that moves from his classic tone to sweeter-toothed euphoria. It’s a colossal mix with industrial throughline, proof of Function’s staying power as one of techno’s greats.

title: Sol Ortega – HATE Podcast 479
artist: Sol Ortega Show: Sol Ortega – HATE Podcast 479 Serie: HATE Podcast Added: March 8, 2026 Genre: Techno
tracklist: Sol Ortega is the 479th guest of our original HATE Podcast series.

A versatile ride through deep and dub textures, flowing into proper techno, with stops along the way in house, Detroit techno and hardgroove territory. There’s a clear thread running through the whole mix: steady groove, jacking hi-hats, and chords that lock in the identity from start to finish.

Born and raised in Buenos Aires, Sol has become one of the few Latin American artists to carve out a strong presence on the global electronic music scene. Her unique sets — skillfully moving along the border between House and Techno — quickly gained traction in Argentina.

Sol has performed at some of the world’s most respected clubs and festivals, including Berghain, Concrete, Fusion Festival, Creamfields, EDC, Stone Techno Festival, Toffler, Boiler Room, Dekmantel, Fabric London, Fabrik, Lollapalooza, among many others.

Her studio work mirrors her approach as a DJ: one step at a time, with unwavering consistency. Early releases on Rhythm Nation and Unitas Multiplex laid the groundwork, while 2023 marked a milestone with her standout release on CROWD, followed by contributions to the Hardproof series on IMF, SEVEN, RAW. Her latest EP ’Auguria’ (2026), was released on Mitsubasa. Whether played by a House or a Techno DJ, Sol’s productions thrive in any context — balancing complexity and simplicity with a rare and distinctive touch.

title: Terminal V Podcast 109 – TJADE
artist: Tjade Show: Terminal V Podcast 109 – TJADE Serie: terminal-v Added: March 6, 2026 Genre: House , Tech House
tracklist: If you’ve spent any time in Europe’s underground dance circuit over the past decade, you’ll have surely heard of Tjade. Amsterdam-born and floor-focused, he’s always defining his own brand of high-energy dancefloor music and blurring the lines between uplifting prog house and early trance. His tracks have blown up on cult labels like Bordello a Parigi, DGTL and Correspondant, and he also heads up Agrio Tracks, a place where emerging talents feel at home.

We caught up with him to talk about the highs and lows of hitting the road, running a label in 2026, crafting nuanced sets that still hit hard, and his vision for a year of more sun-soaked grooves, musicality, and straight-up joy on the dancefloor. Dig in while giving yourself over to his sleek, bouncy and emotionally charged mix, which features cuts from the likes of In2pol & Entasia, Palmiz & Flor Coto and even one of his own.

title: Mees Salomé – Distant 104
artist: Mees Salomé Show: Mees Salomé – Distant 104 Serie: Distant Added: March 6, 2026 Genre: Melodic House , Melodic Techno , Progressive House
genre: Melodic House , Melodic Techno , Progressive House
tracklist: I’ve been working on a lot of exciting things lately. The kind of projects that make you want to rush through and skip to the good part. Working through all those different projects and tasks, I notice like I’m running on autopilot. I seem focused, like getting loads more done in less time, but honestly, I’m just way more impatient than usual. My attention span has shrunk and it feels almost impossible to really sit down with something. Whether that’s work, or me trying not to work.

I can see where all of this is heading, and it looks incredible. I just want it to be here already. The process feels like it’s in the way. Which it isn’t, of course. If I want to do this right, and I really do, then rushing through it would just mean arriving somewhere I’m not fully proud of. It’s more important to do it right than to do it quickly. I have to keep reminding myself of that, and try to slow down enough to actually be present for it.
So maybe we start here. Try to listen through this month’s episode as a whole. No skipping, no shuffling. Just sit down with it, let it play, and see where it takes you. Hope you enjoy ❤️
ps. one of these tracks will be released in 3 weeks.

tracklist: Dance TV is proud to present Dance TV DJ Mix #671 with the Casablanca based DJ, producer and AVGD Records label owner – Kali G. A true architect of the Moroccan underground, he brings over two decades of experience shaped across global dancefloors, with releases on respected international labels and a vision rooted in deep, forward-thinking sounds. As the force behind Avangardis and his newly launched AVGD Records, Kali G continues to build platforms that support and evolve the culture from within.
For this mix, he delivers a fluid, tripped-out and forward-driving journey — guided by subtle energy, intricate melodies, and a hypnotic flow that draws you deeper with every transition. Enjoy!

Kali G (Khalil Belamallem) is a Moroccan DJ, producer, and entrepreneur with more than 25 years deep in the electronic music scene. Widely regarded as one of the key figures behind Morocco’s underground movement, he has played an essential role in shaping and elevating the culture both locally and on an international level.

His journey began in Spain, where he honed his sound and developed a distinct musical identity before taking it worldwide. From Ibiza to Germany, Switzerland, India, Colombia, and Brazil, Kali G has consistently delivered his signature blend of deep, driving grooves to dancefloors across the globe.

On the production front, his work has landed on respected labels such as Windhorse Records, Celo Records, Akbal Music, Achat Records, and Rewire Muzik, further solidifying his presence within the global circuit.

Beyond the booth, he is the founder of Avangardis — a platform focused on artist booking and event production — reflecting his long-term vision of nurturing and expanding electronic and live music culture. Now stepping into a new phase, he launches AVGD Records, an independent label dedicated to forward-thinking sounds, raw underground energy, and authentic artistic expression.
With decades of experience, global reach, and a clear artistic direction, Kali G continues to evolve — pushing boundaries as a DJ, producer, and curator committed to the deeper side of the culture.

title: Data Transmission Podcast 948 – Très Mortimer
artist: Très Mortimer Show: Data Transmission Podcast 948 – Très Mortimer Serie: Data Transmission Podcast Added: March 4, 2026 Genre: House , Tech House , Techno
tracklist: Chicago’s Très Mortimer lands on the Data Transmission podcast this week, fresh from dropping his ‘PRADA’ release on his own Optics Records and bringing a mix packed with unreleased fire.

The Optics boss has been carving out his own lane in recent years, pushing groove-led house rooted in Chicago tradition but built for modern floors. With releases across labels like Ministry of Sound, Mad Decent and Three Six Zero, plus support from the likes of Seth Troxler, BLOND:ISH and Diplo, Mortimer’s records have been doing damage from rooftops to sweaty basements.

His mix for DT gives a proper snapshot of where his head’s at right now. The opener sets the tone straight away with his unreleased collaboration with Geo Smith, ‘Bass Controller’, a track he recently tested in New York and describes as “dancefloor certified.” It’s a chunky, groove-heavy start that rolls straight into cuts from Life on Planets and Jansons, DMX Krew, CASSIMM and Kolter.

There are a couple more unreleased moments in there too, including JAKKOB’s ‘DO YOU UNDERSTAND ME?’, while the middle section lifts off with a mash-up of Maori and OMRI’s ‘Levitate’ layered with Future, Metro Boomin, Playboi Carti and Travis Scott’s ‘Type Shit’.

Naturally, Très Mortimer’s own ‘PRADA (Hans Extended Mix)’ makes an appearance. It’s his favourite moment in the mix and a darker flip of the record, driven by heavy basslines and late-night pressure. That bassline approach is a big part of his style too, he prefers grooves that skip the first beat, leaving space for the drums to punch through and keep the floor moving.
The mix wraps with club-ready cuts from Gabss, Méssous and Kolter, keeping the groove locked all the way through.
Next up, Mortimer is gearing up for a big hometown moment with ARC Festival in Chicago, with the announcement landing soon.

artist: Sebastiaan Hooft Show: Sebastiaan Hooft – The Midnight Project 196 Serie: The Midnight Project Added: March 4, 2026 Genre: Tech House , Techno
tracklist: It’s Wednesday, 6 AM, and episode 196 of The Midnight Project is live. This week is about momentum, unity, and that shared pulse that connects us wherever you’re tuning in from. When you press play, you are stepping into a global circle of dedicated Midnighters who live and breathe this sound together.

We open strong with Pablo Say’s VIP on Truesoul, setting a deep and driving tone right from the first kick. Bart Skils and Weska lift the intensity with For The Music on Drumcode, a title that says everything about why we gather here every week.

Very early in the episode, you’ll hear something personal. Pablo Say and Anna Tur – My Life in my Private Edit. I reshaped this one especially for you. It is emotional, hypnotic, and built to pull us deeper into the journey as one.

Victor Ruiz and Moreira bring the heat with FREAK OUT on Arcane, while UMEK delivers pure energy with The World of Rave. There is a beautiful tension in Detune Prayer by IN-sane and a cosmic drive in Andromeda by Andres Koller and Lautaro Gabioud.

This week’s Classic of the Week is Twin Freaks by The Gateway Experience. This track has that timeless edge. It still feels dangerous, still feels fresh, and it reminds us where this underground spirit comes from. When it drops, you can feel the roots of the culture that shaped us.

In the final stretch, Aundreja’s Adrenaline pushes the pace higher, GP4S hits hard with The World Has Died, and Marie Vaunt closes the episode with a powerful triple on Arcane: Like a Fool, My Prada, and Never Gonna Stop. That closing sequence is relentless and unapologetic.

The Midnight Project airs every Wednesday at 6 AM and later connects with 60,000 listeners on DI.FM. And don’t forget, Saturday at 6 AM, the exclusive guest mix goes live on my channels. We keep building all week long.

Midnighters, this is more than a radio show. It is a growing global family. Share the episode with a friend who needs this energy. Message me your favorite moment. Let’s expand this movement and keep supporting the artists who shape our sound.

artist: GNMR , Zurkin Show: Zurkin b2b GNMR – Bassiani Podcast 299 Serie: Bassiani Podcast Added: March 4, 2026 Genre: Tech House , Techno
tracklist: Up next comes a three-hour bout of hammering beats courtesy of Georgian DJ Zurkin and Italian DJ/Producer GNMR. The Vodkast record founder brings his narrative-driven approach and mastetful mixing style once more, merging leftfield house music with minimal trance and under the radar techno in a seamless exploration of rare record finds and freshly cut dubplates, setting him apart as a versatile and astute DJ. Gianmaria Coccoluto steps up to the task too with his own track selection, one that offers a brand of bubbling rhythms that owes a heavy debt to his DJ father, who set him on an early path as DJ at a mere 14 years old. Worthy of note is his parallel path as recording artist and founder of no less than three music labels: starting with The Dub Rec alongside his father, he later launched his own imprints, Tête Records first and Dubblack.ltd in 2022. This highly charged set weaves together two visions for the club floor, saturated and forward-pitched rhythms that bring something fresh to the table. It’s a pairing that makes a lot of sense, one that generates a mix of primetime cuts that resonates long past night’s end. Bassiani Podcast 299 is a b2b outing from the Horoom floor recorded live on NYE 2026.

title: Art Alfie – Bassiani Podcast 298
artist: Art Alfie Show: Art Alfie – Bassiani Podcast 298 Serie: Bassiani Podcast Added: February 27, 2026 Genre: Tech House , Techno
tracklist: With cheeky beats and firm roots in the dance floor, Oscar Wedren, AKA Art Alfie is a Stockholm talent steeped in his local scene and ready to take on the world. It was in hardcore and psychedelic bands that Wedren kicked off his career, a move from which has deeply influenced his approach to music today. He’s head of Velvet Pony, a self-run imprint with productions that bring a left-field edge to your typical house; worthy of note too, is his long standing collaboration with Mr.Tophat, and the numerous releases on their shared Karlovak imprint. As for his own work, as well as his sets, the name of the game is warm, rolling and melodic sounds that meander light-heartedly along and mix in playful samples with a dose of expertly programmed percussions. 2017 saw his album Reveries Of on Axel Boman, Petter Nordqvist and Kornél Kovács’ Studio Barnhus too, a conduit for catchy, rolling rhythms straight out of downtown Stockholm. With his house-focussed workouts, Wedren brings a chipper flavour to the club and studio that calls forth the energy of Sweden’s off-the-beaten-path approach to parties. Here for Bassiani Podcast 298, comes an hour-long dose of Alfie’s jolly rhythms, breezy sounds for long-awaited sunny days.

tracklist: Dance TV is proud to present a special Dance TV DJ Mix #670 with Bulgarian underground mainstay Nikk., now based in Lille, France 🇫🇷 — a master of refined selection and seamless long-form storytelling, known for his precise mixing technique and deeply curated sound.

Recorded live at Maloot in Lille, this extended 4.5-hour journey dives deep into rolling minimal, stripped-back grooves and immersive deep house textures — a hypnotic ride built on subtle transitions and atmospheric flow. Lock in and let this one unfold!

A cornerstone of the Bulgarian scene for nearly two decades, Nikk. has been shaping dancefloors since 2005 with a sound rooted in minimal, dub house, and organic rhythms. From iconic venues across Sofia to international appearances, his sets are known for their depth, patience, and finely tuned energy. Beyond the booth, he’s released on labels such as Thanq, Baile Musik, Raw Roots, and PL7, while also playing alongside respected names across the global underground circuit such as Fabio Florido, Jun Akimoto, Reelow, Dean Barred, Yvo Zanev, Proudly People, tINI, Matt Sassari, Spartaque, Skober, Nakadia, Hollen, Franz Costa, D-Formation or Paco Maroto. Last but not least being a professional at all he touches, Nikk. is also an integral member of the Dance TV team, guarding the quality of audio and video as our irreplaceable Content Manager.
Now entering a new chapter from Lille, Nikk. continues to evolve his sound — and this recording captures exactly that.

title: Sebastiaan Hooft – The Midnight Project 195
artist: Sebastiaan Hooft Show: Sebastiaan Hooft – The Midnight Project 195 Serie: The Midnight Project Added: February 25, 2026 Genre: Tech House , Techno
tracklist: Episode 195 is here, and this one hits with pure drive from the very first kick. I built this week’s journey around control, tension, and release, that feeling when the groove locks in and you forget everything else around you. Whether you tuned in on Wednesday at 6 AM CET or caught it later on DI.FM with 60,000 global listeners, you know this one was made to move.

We open strong with Serioes, Legendaer, and Little Duracell’s Take Control (Return Fall Extended Remix), setting the tone with a deep but commanding pulse. Patrick Scuro, The Post Brothers, and The Enveloper keep the pressure high with Oldschool, while Zafer Atabey’s Unrest on EXTIMA brings that hypnotic tension I love to play with early in the set.

Crossbow and GIULIA (IT) take us inward with Someone in the Mirror before YellowHeads unleash Monochrome Dreams in Peak Mode, a serious moment on the dancefloor. Then UMEK drops Kappa One… and you already know that means business.

Mid-set, Salkantay’s Cross The Line and Nicolas Hoop with BCT’s Mental Focus push the groove into overdrive. Victor Ruiz and HNGT’s A New Day on 1001 Recordings lifts the energy beautifully, and Layton Giordani with Camden Cox on Destiny adds that emotional edge that keeps things human inside the machine.

The final stretch is where it gets special. Victor Ruiz and Moreira’s Every Day Arcane flows into Liberthorn’s Digital Dissociative, and then we flip it. L.A. Style’s James Brown is Dead in UMEK’s bootleg form is a nod to the roots, reimagined for now. Annie Hill closes Episode 195 with Legacy, and that title says it all.
This show is about pushing forward while respecting where we came from. New names, established legends, exclusive heat, all in one uninterrupted ride.
Thank you for being part of this movement every single week. Your energy fuels The Midnight Project, and I feel it wherever I play.
See you next Wednesday at 6 AM.

title: Data Transmission Podcast 947 – Joey London Style
artist: Joey London Style Show: Data Transmission Podcast 947 – Joey London Style Serie: Data Transmission Podcast Added: February 23, 2026 Genre: House , Tech House , Techno
show: Data Transmission Podcast 947 – Joey London Style
tracklist: Joey London Style steps up for Data Transmission as his ‘Clurb’ EP lands on Hottrax this January.

Fresh from his latest outing on Jamie Jones’ label, the London-raised, Manchester-based selector delivers a mix stacked with groove and intent. ‘Clurb’ and ‘Little Bitter’ both feature, with the latter his personal pick, and you can hear why. Tough drums. Weighty low-end. Built for busy rooms.

There’s plenty of Joey London Style dubs in here too. ‘Copy Kats’, ‘HOT GIRL CRAZY’, ‘The Speed Train’ and ‘Grip Tight’ all get a run out, sitting alongside cuts from Joe Thomas, Ruggier and Baylee Brown. It moves fast. It keeps its punch. No filler.
If you’ve been following his rise through Hottrax, Cuttin’ Headz and Metamorfosi, this feels like another clear step forward. Focused, confident and very much aimed at peak-time.
Stream the full Joey London Style mix now on Data Transmission and grab ‘Clurb’ via Hottrax on 23rd January.

tracklist: Dance TV is proud to present Dance TV DJ Mix #669 with Mexico City–born, Puebla-based DJ and producer ViiV — a rising force within Mexico’s underground whose refined taste and vinyl-driven sets have quietly earned her a respected place behind the decks. Viiv reinforces a reputation built not on excess, but on patience, musicality, and an instinctive understanding of atmosphere — qualities that position her among the new generation carrying the underground forward. Check out her sublime, deep and eclectic vinyl only DJ mix for Dance TV! Enjoy!

Mexico City–born, Puebla-based DJ and producer Vivian Garciaferro aka ViiV is a rising force within Mexico’s underground electronic scene. Her refined taste and vinyl-driven sets have quietly earned her a respected place behind the decks. Active since the early 2010s, Viiv’s artistic path deepened during a formative period in Chicago, where full immersion in the city’s legendary house ecosystem helped shape her musical identity and led her to become part of the Naughty Bad Fun Collective, founded by Sassmouth.

A dedicated crate digger with a clear affinity for the tactile ritual of vinyl, ViiV is known for crafting elegant journeys through minimal house and techno — subtle, hypnotic, and rich in detail. Her commitment to the format translates into sets that feel intentional and deeply curated, balancing restraint with groove while allowing the music’s textures to breathe. This approach has brought her to some of the country’s most respected clubs and stages, including appearances at Boiler Room and Comunité Festival, where her understated confidence and selector’s mindset have resonated with discerning dancefloors.

Beyond the booth, ViiV continues to expand her footprint in the underground by spreading a distinct whim — capricho — energy through her projects and collaborations. She is not only a resident of Sonoro, but als of Space Container, a new party in CDMX focused on merging forward-thinking electronic music with high-quality visual experiences, creating immersive environments that go beyond the dancefloor. With original productions currently in the works and the forthcoming launch of her Unisono label, ViiV is stepping into a new chapter — one that blends sound, vision, and intention while staying rooted in the deeper shades of the underground.

title: Sebastiaan Hooft – The Midnight Project 194
artist: Sebastiaan Hooft Show: Sebastiaan Hooft – The Midnight Project 194 Serie: The Midnight Project Added: February 18, 2026 Genre: Tech House , Techno
tracklist: Episode 194 is live, and this week is a true showcase of the artists driving the culture forward right now. Every Wednesday at 6 AM we connect across time zones, and I am proud of the names featured in this one.

We open with Adam Sellouk and Alex Kaspersky on Drumcode. Adam has been on a serious rise, appearing on major lineups worldwide and building a reputation that goes far beyond the studio. KASIA continues to establish herself as one of the strongest forces in the current wave of producers, and her collaboration with KAF3R reflects that growing international presence. Township Rebellion and Fab Massimo represent consistency at the highest level, with Township in particular remaining a staple across global festivals and clubs.

Zafer Atabey is another artist to watch closely. His work on EXTIMA shows how fast new names are stepping into the spotlight. And then there is UMEK. A true pillar of the scene. Decades deep and still leading from the front. His influence on generations of producers is undeniable.

Roddy Lima’s connection with Drumcode continues to strengthen his profile, while MIRA MIRA, VE/RA, and Paula van Klar are part of a powerful new generation claiming their space. It is important to me that The Midnight Project gives that platform to rising artists alongside established names.

Cherrymoon Trax and Thomas Schumacher represent history and legacy. Bringing that 1994 anthem back into rotation is about respect for where this culture began. Thomas has consistently remained relevant through evolution, and that longevity deserves recognition.

Return Fall and Chris Mantanz are building momentum, Shuhandz, NYMESYS, and Nicole Chen show how collaboration fuels growth, and Marie Vaunt continues her unstoppable climb with major international recognition. Closing with Storm and Juliet Fox connects two strong artistic identities, and Juliet remains one of the most respected names on global lineups.
This is what Episode 194 stands for. Established icons, rising talent, and artists who are shaping what we will be hearing in clubs worldwide.
Thank you for being part of this movement. Your energy keeps this platform alive.
See you next Wednesday at 6 AM.

title: Dold – Bassiani Podcast 297
artist: Dold Show: Dold – Bassiani Podcast 297 Serie: Bassiani Podcast Added: February 18, 2026 Genre: Tech House , Techno
tracklist: Bridging emotionally charged sounds with driving loops of the highest order, Patrik Eriksson has cast a striking form in Sweden and beyond. Since his 2015 founding of Arsenik Records (alongside Kuf), the nordic phenom has expanded his catalogue and scope to include live sets as well as studio productions, both demonstrating a deep passion for music as well as a tightly focused reinterpretation of what came before. As Dold, he pulls from IDM, ambient, electro and techno and reformulates a percussive hallmark brimming with mechanical intensity, one that swells with ideas and a technical skill that raises the bar record on record; his latest for instance is a heavy-duty banger titled Feng Shui, a VA contribution worthy of his name. From Europe to farther afield his sets too, negotiate the twin demands of mind and body, offering a highly intelligent and highly danceable techno forever at the vanguard. For Bassiani Podcast 297 Dold returns with yet another masterclass in expert mixing, a 90 minute rollercoaster through contemporary rhythms and nordic ambiance recorded in his Stockholm studio.

title: Data Transmission Podcast 946 – Josh Hvaal
artist: Josh Hvaal Show: Data Transmission Podcast 946 – Josh Hvaal Serie: Data Transmission Podcast Added: February 16, 2026 Genre: House , Tech House , Techno
tracklist: Josh Hvaal steps up for DT Podcast 946 with a 100% JHV Mix, and it lands heavy.

Eight releases deep with Jamie Jones and his Hot Creations camp, Josh Hvaal has moved from breakthrough name to reliable club weapon. From ‘The Sound EP’ through to a steady run of dancefloor records, he’s earned backing from heads like Patrick Topping, Joseph Capriati, Solomun and Pete Tong. Not by accident. The tunes work.

This week’s mix says it plainly. A journey through the sound of a 100% JHV Mix. Fourteen tracks. All Josh Hvaal. Around 75% unreleased. No filler, no detours. Just rolling drums, tight low end and that clipped vocal energy he’s dialled in over the last few years.

There’s weight in the IDs. You can hear the next six months taking shape. ‘Where Ya Been Baby’ and ‘Rhythm Of House’ bring that direct, peak-time bounce. ‘Want 2 Feel’ locks into a groove that feels built for low ceilings and warm rooms. And then there’s ‘Hustlers Dance’, the standout and Josh Hvaal’s personal favourite in the mix.

‘Hustlers Dance’ drops Friday 13th February on Trick, the label run by Patrick Topping. It’s one he’s been working towards for a while, and you can hear why. It’s sharp. Confident. Built for those moments when the floor is already moving and you just need to push it further.

Josh Hvaal has been steadily building his own lane too with Gibberish, unveiled by Pete Tong on BBC Radio 1, and that same drive runs through this hour. It feels focused. No hype. Just club music made by someone who spends time in clubs.
DT Podcast 946 is a marker. A snapshot of where Josh Hvaal is right now, and where he’s heading next.
Lock into the full 100% JHV Mix, and keep ‘Hustlers Dance’ on your radar this Friday.

title: Blasha & Allatt – HATE Podcast 476
artist: Blasha & Allatt Show: Blasha & Allatt – HATE Podcast 476 Serie: HATE Podcast Added: February 15, 2026 Genre: Techno
tracklist: Blasha & Allatt are the 476th guests of our original HATE Podcast series.
A high energy club mix by Blasha & Allatt that sees the duo blending hypnotic grooves with raw machine funk that’ll keep you locked from start to finish 🔐

Blasha & Allatt are honorary Mancunian DJs and co-founders of the renowned Meat Free parties, celebrated as some of the wildest techno raves in the UK. Known for their magnetic energy behind the decks, the duo have built a strong reputation both locally and across Europe, bringing intensity and connection to every set, whether at The White Hotel, Blitz or Bret.

Their sound moves seamlessly between techno and house, a dynamic force that has lit up clubs like FOLD, Berghain and Radion, as well as festivals including Stone Techno, Awakenings and Dekmantel. In 2022 they joined Amsterdam’s Vault Sessions as residents, deepening their bond with the city’s scene while continuing to shape Manchester’s underground.
With releases on Blue Hour, Positive Source, Discos Paraiso and Symbolism, Blasha & Allatt continue to evolve, driven by community, creativity and an unshakable love for the dance floor.

title: Monument Techno Podcast 506 – Síoda Rua
artist: Unknown
show: Monument Techno Podcast 506 – Síoda Rua Serie: Monument Techno Podcast Added: February 12, 2026 Genre: Techno
tracklist: Síoda Rua is a Berlin-based DJ originally from Ireland. She has enjoyed a lifelong connection to music, rooted in years of playing classical and Irish traditional instruments, which eventually led her into the electronic scene.

Prior to settling in Berlin, she spent nearly a decade immersed in the Parisian scene, followed by a year touring across Mexico — chapters that helped refine her sound and broaden her artistic perspective.
Regarding the mix Síoda offered some thoughts :

‘ This two hour vinyl mix is a showcase of the sound I feel most connected to right now. I wanted to build a journey into those hypnotic spaces, the kind of music that feels like being lost in a mystical forest. It is a place where I feel a real sense of freedom, allowing me to let go and lose myself in the music.

Deep hypnotic techno has always been what I have been drawn to, but I’ve also developed a love for the tribal aspects of the music I play. It reminds me of my time living in Chiapas, a part of Mexico where the Mayan culture is still so present. That region has a deep connection to psychedelics and ancient rituals, which influenced my more recent dive into the trippy and trancey style of certain tracks I select. This mix is a reflection of that journey and the sounds that move me.’

title: Sebastiaan Hooft – The Midnight Project 193
artist: Sebastiaan Hooft Show: Sebastiaan Hooft – The Midnight Project 193 Serie: The Midnight Project Added: February 11, 2026 Genre: Tech House , Techno
tracklist: Welcome back to The Midnight Project. This week’s episode kicks off a special run that’s very close to my heart. Dark, driving, and locked into a deep late-night flow, this one is all about momentum and trust in the groove.

I opened the show with “Ritmolicious,” taken from a brand-new four-track EP that UMEK just sent me. This is the first track from that release, and I’ll be featuring the remaining three cuts across the next three episodes of The Midnight Project. No rush, no shortcuts. Each track gets its own moment and its own space exactly where it belongs.

Around that exclusive opener, the energy builds with powerful selections from Emmanuel Miro, Nikoretti, C-Poch, and Return Fall, followed by a timeless, remastered weapon from Monika Kruse and Voodooamt. The second half of the show keeps the pressure high with music from Rich Coote, German Carrizo, ZEREN, Nico Banfi with Techmo, CHANCEKNOT, YellowHeads, and Ali James, carrying us through to the closing moments.
This is what The Midnight Project is about. Sharing new music directly from the artists, giving it room to breathe, and taking you along for the journey as it unfolds week by week.
Thank you for tuning in, for listening closely, and for being part of this every Wednesday morning. I’ll see you next week at 6 AM for the next chapter.

title: Simone de kunovich – Bassiani Podcast 296
artist: Simone De Kunovich Show: Simone de kunovich – Bassiani Podcast 296 Serie: Bassiani Podcast Added: February 11, 2026 Genre: Tech House , Techno
tracklist: Meet Simone de Kunovich, Italian DJ and producer with an eclectic approach to electronic music. International resident of Public Records in New York and Minh in Hong Kong, as well as Love on the Rocks family member, he spent the past two decades accumulating a gigantic collection that spans across records, books, synths, movie posters and collectible of all sorts. He’s a house aficionado, everything from deep to tech house and weirder avantgarde inflections (like his Mondo Nuovo trilogy on Japanese publisher Mule Musiq, influenced by 60/70s avantgarde cinema soundtracks): it’s dance music with a wealth of cultural touchpoints behind it, underlined by extensive crate digging and an intuitive feel for rhythm. For this latest Podcast number, Simone delves back into that universe and returns hands full with a patient assemblage, rolling and funky through and through. Bassiani Podcast 296 is a three hour edition from the Horoom floor, packed with bouncing baselines and saccharine tunes, feel-good house from an Italian master recorded live at Bassiani’s anniversary back in October.

tracklist: Shortly after making his debut on International Deejay Gigolos back in 2000, Poladroïd ventured on his own to establish Roulette Rekordz. He then toured Europe performing in cities such as Madrid, Barcelona, London, Amsterdam, Prague, Paris… and predominantly in Belgium alongside artists like ADULT., Ectomorph, Dopplereffekt, Luke Eargoggle, MANASYt, Zerkalo and numerous local talents where he has gained a reputation for his dynamic and energetic live performances, delivering a unique blend of electro with an unwavering intensity that has remained consistent throughout the years.

Around 2008 the label ceased its activities and shortly after Poladroïd took a break from his musical pursuits. However, he resurfaced in 2019, simultaneously relaunching his label. Since then he has released music on Science Cult, Detriti, Microm, Applied Research, Meta Moto, Diffuse Reality, Patterned Media… In addition to his work as Poladroïd, he has also released albums as the Xenomorph Jazz Ensemble and under the Cercle Futur moniker.

tracklist: Josh Heywood is the 475th guest of our original HATE Podcast series.
A key figure in Australia’s techno circuit, Josh Heywood crafts his sets instinctively, always guided by the dancefloor.

This set truly represents Josh as an artist, diving deep into a steady pulse. It’s meditative yet physical, blurring time, keeping bodies moving, and suspending minds somewhere between focus and release. Josh is known for his driven, immersive techno, combining driving rhythms, dark textures, and layered mixing. His releases have appeared on respected & influential European labels, translating seamlessly across clubs and late-night dancefloors.

tracklist: Enjoy this week’s episode with Colombian NY House Music Legend DJ & Producer JOESKI. Change is inevitable, and nowhere is this more prevalent than in the world of dance music. Analog gives way to digital, trends come and go, yet NYC’s DJ Joeski remains at the top of his game, and now, in the midst of his fourth decade as one of house music’s most sought-after stars, his momentum shows no signs of slowing. Joeski’s trajectory can be traced back to 1991, when he burst onto the NYC house music scene as a founding member of The Chocolate Factory DJ collective. He delighted crowds at Limelight, Tunnel, Palladium and NASA, helped turn “Save The Robots” into a NYC afterhours institution and earned his first residency at “Together” parties at the legendary Roxy, playing alongside the likes of Danny Tenaglia, Louie Vega and Roger Sanchez. Fueled by his genuine love of the music & his hard work through the years, there’s no doubt that Joeski will continue to play a major role in this industry. tracklist: Dance TV is proud to present Dance TV DJ Mix #668 with Egyptian-born DJ, producer, and tastemaker Shadi Megallaa, whose journey from New York and the UK to Dubai has established him as a key figure in the city’s electronic music culture. A longtime underground devotee and respected community builder, he is the force behind Ark To Ashes and founder of The Flip Side Dubai record shop — both reflecting his commitment to musical integrity and his mission to make house deep again. Drawing from a broad spectrum of house, techno, and beyond, Shadi delivers immersive, groove-led soundscapes shaped by refined taste, deep knowledge, and decades of dedication to the craft. Enjoy this dope mix!

Egyptian-born DJ, producer, and tastemaker Shadi Megallaa is a true underground lifer whose journey through electronic music has taken him from New York and the UK to Dubai, where he has become a pivotal figure in shaping the city’s evolving dance music culture. With decades of dedication behind him, Megallaa embodies the ethos of the underground — a friend to many, an enemy of none, and an artist driven by an enduring mission to make house deep again.

As the founder of Ark To Ashes record label and the driving force behind The Flip Side record shop — now a cornerstone for vinyl collectors and discerning selectors in the region — his influence extends far beyond the DJ booth. Both platforms reflect his unwavering commitment to nurturing community, preserving musical integrity, and supporting forward-thinking artists.

Rooted in the foundations of house, techno, and adjacent sonic territories, Shadi draws on a wealth of experience, diverse taste, and a finely tuned ear to craft productions and DJ sets that resonate with depth and purpose. His sound is immersive yet precise — layered with groove, subtle emotion, and understated power — capturing the essence of a culture he has long helped cultivate while continuing to push it forward.
